reviews.review:
Went here solo while fam was at a basketball game.  Sat at tall chairs at kitchen counter of small restaurant.  Great service with recommendations of spanish mackerel crudo as well as pommes with uni which was potato cake topped with uni. I probably wouldnt have ordered this but for recommendation but i loved it the flavors and textures blended great.  Crudo was good made with oil so a little different than i expected.  

My fave thing i had was the beef tartar.  Perfect balance flavor and texture.  I loved it and cant wait to go back.  

Also had a mezcal Negroni and it was awesome too.

tasty food in a little wine bar. the kimchi pithivier was the star of the meal, would get one for myself next time. radishes and butter were ok, the crudo was solid, the eclair was good but expected a bit more of a salty punch, and the pommes darphin was good as well but thought the uni serving was on the smaller end and the flavor didn't come through enough against the potatoes and relish

Pleasantly surprised. New american often disappoints, but this did not. If you have to order one thing, get the Pissaladiéclair. Anchovies and Olives in an eclair-like pastry--so delicious!

Oh also get the Sourdough! The bread was delicious as well.

I wouldn't recommend it to a friend. I think maybe the problem is that you should not go here as a solo dinner sitting at one of the four counter stools, even with reservation for that. 

I felt like either an afterthought or that I was the only person there who's not a regular customer. They various guys who put the plates in front of me didn't seem excited by it, like when you go through a drive-through window.
Delicious and interesting dishes. Unique flavors and beautiful presentation. A must-try.

The servers were really nice but the food is genuinely awful. It was a surreal experience, we asked for the check and left half way through to go eat at another restaurant- super disappointing and the biggest waste of money.
Had an amazing dinner at Wildair with wonderful accommodating service from Hannah!! She guided our experience in a beautiful way and the dishes were impeccable. Will absolutely dine again!

author.name: Pelle M.
author.location: Lower East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review:
Wildair is always a genuine treat. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable which are equally important when there's such a long and interesting wine list to be shown around. The vibes are good although I recommend a table if you can get it over the counter seating up against the wall that can feel a little cramped. 

The main attraction manages to be the food which is an achievement when the wine offerings are as good as they are here. On our latest visit, we had the Thon Mayo which was rich and tasty and cut with the right amount of acid, oysters that were delicious in their own but also nicely adorned with artichoke and infused oil, the pig's head sandwich that was a delight, the pithivier which was a standout for the flakey pastry, tasty melty cheese and a nice little zip from the kimchi, and the pommes dauphin with uni that is basically the perfect thing--crispy potato matched up with creamy uni? Come on. The mille feuille was crisp, flakey, creamy with a meringue that just melted away. Super way to cap off a great meal. 

Minor gripe: the pacing of our latest meal was off. The Thon Mayo came out quick and we managed to polish it off and have a breather before the oysters arrived, but the pommes, pithivier and pigs head sandwich all came within minutes of each other so couldn't be enjoyed at their hot fresh peak, which is important when delicious melty cheese and crispy potato are involved. The upshot of this was also that we finished 5 savory dishes within an hour of sitting down which felt a bit rushed. Maybe order two cold things and one hot then regroup and carry on.

The line at 11:30 am for their weekend donuts is absolutely worth the hype. At $9.50/donut, these behemoths are roughly the size of 2-3 donuts and packed with flavor. I tried two inventive flavors:  malted milkshake with amaretto cherry on top and pistachio almond. The pistachio almond had this brilliant combination of crumble and icing on top that tasted so nostalgic. The malted pastry cream in the milkshake donut was delightful.

Two people could easily split one donut. I had leftovers for several days.  

They should offer a utensils and a napkin with the donut given the high cost/sticky factor.

Star rating is based on value for money.  When I ordered the most expensive thing on the menu ($35), I expected a truly decadent meticulous and fully developed dish.  Instead I got a greasy hashbrown thrown on an empty plate with some flavorless "relish" that you could barely taste and a slight seafood aftertaste.  So weird and disappointing and SO EXPENSIVE.  I didn't even have anyone come ask me if it was any good.  I would have been honest with them about it.  Also got the sourdough bread and it was pretty good, but a bummer to have to pay $6 for it instead of it being complimentary when the rest of the dishes are so overpriced.  The menu is pretty limited too, so this will probably be my last time trying this spot,  such a disappointment.  And (did I mention?) expensive!

Such a great restaurant. Relaxed, casual, and yet so sophisticated. I ate there a while back, but came across my picture of their clam dish, so I felt inspired to find a great review. Everything in ate was delicious, the staff was great, and while the simple decor wouldn't expose their upscale quality, it really IS upscale in very humble manner. Love it.

If you like donuts, you must venture here at 12 pm on Saturday! We came for the black and white donut at 1215 (but was sold out, it goes quick!) and got the mango cheesecake instead. The inside had two layers - mango cream and cheesecake (?). It was amazing! A bit on the pricier side, but definitely worth the visit.

Donut review because HOLY cannoli they makes some freaking awesome donuts. Don't sleep on this place: get there by 1140 and wait for perfection. By the time 12 pm rolls in, if you try to get in line then, you will be out of luck because the line was 40 people deep by the time the doors open.

We had a yuzu lemon meringue, chocolate peanut butter and a crispy cinnamon roll. The first two were AMAZING. Pillowy, stuffed with creamy goodness, topped with gorgeous fluffy meringue for the first, delectable ganache on the other. The crispy cinnamon roll was like a palmier and while delicious, I'd get more of those yeasted bad boys before getting the crispy variety again.

PLEASE open a standalone donut shop. They are glorious.

Shared a dark chocolate doughnut / beignet with my wife. Had a chocolate cream filling with a dark chocolate glaze and toasted marshmallows on top. Texture was balanced but on the yeasty side. Surprisingly unsweet for a pastry. Quite rich and toasty.

Certainly worth a detour, but sitting at the chef's counter is a must for party of two or alone for a delicious and creative bite (or several). Come for the atmosphere, the cocktails, the food, and the show in the kitchen.

Whoever makes the doughnuts on Saturdays is amazing. Whoever runs it, ruins the entire experience. They run out as soon as they open. It's like they make a total of 5 doughnuts for the day. Wasted my time coming here twice. Don't bother using the Uber eats app because it collapses, since everyone tries to order it at the same time. Why say you're open till 2:30pm when you're sold out at 12:05pm?

Wildair has been on my list to try for a long time and we finally decided to make a reservation. We ordered a bunch of dishes to share and it was hard to narrow it down since everything sounded good. 

Overall, the meal was enjoyable. Loved the topneck clams, oysters and skate wing. And the salad was probably the best one I've had in a long time.

Wasn't a fan of the beef tartare. It was so oily and the portion was too large for only two people. Probably better for a larger group. 

The wine selection was great and had some interesting bottles. Cute date spot!
As tomato lovers we really enjoyed the pan con tomate. We also really liked the panna cotta. They have a great wine selection with a lot of natural wines.

Our group had a late 8:45pm reservation and were seated immediately after arriving. Wildair is a smaller spot in LES, so if you have a larger party (say 5-7 people) make a reservation well in advance.

Since we had a big party, we were able to get a taste of a lot of things. We ordered the little gem salad, oysters, scallop crudo, jerk prawn skewers, pissaladieclair, potato darphin w/ uni. There were a lot of international flavors that the menu was inspired by, namely a lot of Asian flavors (XO sauce in the oysters, uni for the potato, dashi for the scallops) and obviously French cooking techniques. This was pretty interesting to me and had some tasty results. My favs were probably the scallop crudo and pissaladieclair, though most things were quite good--there were a few misses, namely the potato w/ uni. I wish there was a bigger portion of uni--without it, I think the dish was good but a bit plain.

I also appreciated how attentive and accommodating our waiter was when we were trying to choose a wine to pair with our meal. We tried a lot of different types on the menu, and it was nice to take our time. Selection is not super huge but there are some good ones to choose from. 

We got a mille feuille on the house for dessert since they ran out of panna cotta for the night. We had tried ordering beforehand but the order was forgotten by the time we asked for it. The dessert we had was good though. 

Overall not a bad choice for a nice dinner and I enjoyed the food here!

Such a lovely little spot! I was solo which can get a little tricky with small plates, so I didn't get to try as much as I'd like. The clams and tartare were both very good but the standout was the Mille feuille dessert. So many textures, sweet but peppery- I will be thinking about it for a while! Also my server was very knowledgeable about organic wine

We tried it again as friends were interested in going and we were in the neighborhood. Terrible service and the food wasn't hot. Save your money and take it to any number of better places around the corner.

The food is incredible. The staff really knows what's up. The menu is all small dishes and it's definitely very pricey... but absolutely at a Michelin level quality. I believe they have a sister restaurant with a Michelin star. Highlights are the steak tartare and the raw clams!!! I am sure the menu changes often, but when we went there were lots of raw options on the menu... not a vegetarian friendly menu but if you eat fish you are good. The skate was a delightful surprise... deboned and absolutely stunning flavor profile.

One word of caution... we ended up ordering all three desserts expecting them to be the small portion of the other dishes, but it was a little too much dessert, haha!

Came here on a Tuesday night around 630 and it was easy to get a table. I ordered the bread, the gem salad, the tuna and the skate and it was all quite delicious. The portions are not huge so don't come if you're starving but if you're hungry, you'll be satisfied with that many items. At the end, my favorites were the gem salad and the skate which had a bit of a piccata flavor to it. The ambience was OK there's not too much space in the restaurant so if you don't mind sitting next to others in a long table, then you're fine. I don't mind and I think there was enough space between the seats. Luckily the people one seat over were not very loud, so it was no big deal. We were by the front door but luckily it was a 70° day so no issues there. It would have been nice to sit outside but when I was standing in that area, there were a lot of flies so that was a turn off. The service was great. Our server was knowledgeable and kind and we were checked up on a couple times.

I've been here twice, but had two different experiences. My first time visiting was great and I left wanting to return for a full dinner -- I had come for after dinner drinks with my fiancé. We got a bottle of wine and the beef tartare to snack on which was fantastic. The overall service was friendly and attentive, and we were seated immediately upon arriving. It was a great date spot for LES.

My second time visiting wasn't great. We ordered enough courses for 3 people and unfortunately wasn't impressed with the food. We only ordered seafood dishes since we were with someone who didn't eat meat. The potato dauphinoise with uni (most expensive item we ordered) was probably the most underwhelming dish.

The service was also lackluster (not uncommon for a typical NYC restaurants but opposite from the experience we had the first time). We happened to be in the neighborhood early, and decided to stop by to see if they could seat us early. The hostess confirmed that they were (understandably) fully booked until our reservation time so we left and just walked around until our reservation time. We returned at the exact time of our reservation and the hostess mentioned they were still waiting on our table. We waited for about 10 minutes outside and then went back to check in with the hostess on the status who seemed rather bothered that we were checking in. We received the same answer from her (they were still waiting on our table to wrap up). We waited another 5 minutes until the party finally left and the table was cleared. The hostess came out to grab us but offered no apology at all for the delay. I get that it's a busy and popular wine bar (one where you really need to make reservations weeks in advance for prime time on a weekend) but I feel like it's common for restaurants to give tables a heads up that their reservation is coming to an end so they can make sure to seat people on time. The restaurant we had gone to right before (also very busy and popular) had the courtesy to give us a heads up on when they needed the table back so we had enough time to order one more drink + food.

author.name: Nicole G.
author.location: Lower Nob Hill, San Francisco, CA

reviews.review: Boston cream and all other donuts I've gotten lucky enough to try were delectable. Never been for dinner, but love their BEP (pineapple instead of cheese was a wild change but an amazing one).

OK.  If you are having a "top 25" NYC restaurant experience I would not go here.  But I like their social, could watch for dayssssss. A bit of a cluster after all. BE WARNED they close before they say.

It pains me to give this review because I was so excited to eat here. First for the food: the beef tartare was delicious, everything else was relatively forgettable to the point I am struggling to remember what else was on the table. The white mezcal Negroni was also delicious, but the waiter never asked if we wanted another drink and was hard to get attention of so we were limited to one... Unfortunately, the service was just not up to par and had a large effect on the meal. Server was grumpy the whole meal and wasn't willing to make any sort of accommodations (like some extra potatoes on a plate of $165 steak that came with 8 small pieces???). Didn't even try dessert as we were too fed up by that point. Definitely a trendy place with potential (like sister restaurant Contra which we loved) but not a quick return for me.

Fabulous dinner w friends here - great service and the cooking was fantastic. The beef tartare was the best I've ever had. And thankfully they have natural wines that aren't all overly funky. Recommend for a date or a fun eve w friends - definitely fit for foodies!

We had a dinner reservation so no wait. Service was quite good even though we were seated outdoors. 

bread and olive oil - oil is from italy, much more fragrant
topneck clams - one of my favorite dishes here. amazing tasty clam. 
oysters - 6 oysters for $18, delicious pairing 
scallop crudo - one scallop sliced into three pieces. A bit sad to share just 1 scallop for $19
American Wagyu striploin - medium rare steak. i mean it's good but not that great.

Was looking forward to dinner here as I haven't been on the LES in a while. It's very much a young crowd, 20s mostly, so can get loud. Everyone sits closely together in very high chairs. Our waiter suggested sharing four dishes for two people. We ordered five. The pan tomate was very pretty but a bit impractical to eat. The tomato is on the bottom and topped with a thin crisp bread. Cutting into it is a total bummer because the tomato gets squished and the bread cracks in shards. It was seasoned well but hard to get a complete bite. We also ordered the squash blossoms, a tempura type app. It was a bit too much batter for my tastes. The head on shrimp was tasty but I couldn't get my head around eating the shell, which was chewy and uncomfortable. The tuna with peppers was good but not memorable. Potatoes were very crispy and tasty. The uni was a nice touch but didn't add much flavor. The standout was the peach dessert, a creamy, light taste of heaven. If you're in the area, I'd recommend getting a glass of wine and maybe one dish.

Finally got a reservation here on Resy! It was such a vibe - packed and buzzing! Our waiter was hilarious and very appreciated that he paid attention to what was said! 

We couldn't decide between the 2 desserts and asked him to surprise us! He came back around with the Fig Sundae noting that he overheard me sharing that I loved figs! Now that is GRADE A+ Service!

Must Order / My favourites:
1/ Potato Darphin with Uni - Gutted to have to share (kidding, kind of!); That potato cake would be epic for a hangover cure, just sayin'
2/ Jerk Prawn Skewers - Extremely flavourful and super fresh; definitely eat the entire shrimp (the shells are edible!)
3/ Fig Sundae

Other dishes we ordered: 
5/ Pissaladière inside an éclair - This didn't work for me but interesting spin!
6/ Scallops with fried capers - The scallops were a bit fishier than I'd like but paired well with the capers

Definitely a spot that will be repeated.

I always get the dessert here! Found this hidden gem awhile back before it became so popular and have loved it since. Even though the desserts are a bit overpriced, they are worth every penny. They are delicious and have such an unique taste it's wild. 10/10!

This was not our favorite meal in the city unfortunately; nothing was "bad" per se, but we had been excited to try it and it did not live up to expectations. Also: very pricey for what it was.

We came here on Tuesday evening, and what was already thumbs down was that everything was high-top seating, and tables were not only close together but directly on top of each other (we reeeeeallllllly loved overhearing the conversation of the Gen Zers on their first date who were practically sitting in our laps). Cocktails are good (spritz and the G&T). It's small plate-style, so you gotta order and pony up. Some thoughts:
--Bread and olive oil: both good, both nothing you've never seen before
--beef tartare: we're torn about this since one of us really liked it and one of us did not care for it as much because it tasted a bit off to her; it was a unique take on the dish though
--little gem salad: this version was not as good as the one that we had at Mel's the previous night. We loved the dill explosion, but it was VERY lightly dressed and the "sauce" on the bottom wasn't enough for the whole plate.
--Pommes darphin: this pissed us off. It's essentially just a kugel that's been cooked in a cast iron or whatever, so WHY ON EARTH does it cost $36???? Yes, the jalapeño relish was a nice topping, but still--cost, labor, etc. does not justify the cost. 
--Paris brest: ours was a ferrero rocher version. Again, good, but nothing that you haven't had before if you've been around respectable French bakeries.

So, overall, not worth it. Maybe we came here too long after the restaurant peaked, but in our opinion, there are better meals to be had in NYC value- and quality wise.
this stuff is crazy. bonkers, bananas, nuts, loco, insane, synonyms; you know the type.
Excellent little restaurant with creative menu. They have a nice wine selection and the staff is well informed. Although the menu is small, it's easy to keep ordering.

Wildair is a terrific place to enjoy the vibe with creative foods and a lovely boo to match.

- Littleneck Clams: Decorative and refreshing. 
- Pithivier: Tasted like an upscale hot pocket but better because of its flaky pastery. 
- Pissaladiéclair: The anchovies were bold and empowering. It was savory and delicious.
- Stuffed Chicken Wings: Subtle and yet fulfilling - a satisfying take on Asian flavors.
- Mille Feuille: Light, crispy and delectable. The aftertaste had a hint of popcorn which made the feeling nostalgic and elevated at the same time.
 
Looking forward to come back so we can try the rest of the menu. Thanks for having us

Very small and intimate place for drinks and small plates to share. Food was inventive and tasty. I really enjoyed the gin and tonic that they made. It was perfectly balanced. The desserts were creative and delicious. Great place to meet up with friends after work for a light bite and drinks or for a date night.

Things I'd order again:
Granita
Cinnamon Brown Sugar, salted caramel, apply jelly mille feuille
Chicken Wings
Beef Tartare
Bread
Shrimp
Top Neck Clams
Mussels - that sauce was delicious

Most items are from 3 - 38 bucks, but there is a 24oz wagyu on the menu that comes with potatoes and that will set you back only $165.

I've been here twice and although the food has been good, it hasn't wowed me like the other reviews have indicated. The first time we came, we had the roast beef dip sandwich, and it was good, nothing spectacular.  

On this particular visit, we got the dip Pithivier. It was good, but it was certainly a lot more hot and melty in the Instagram photos.  Sadly, there's no sit down, so it was cold by the time we could eat it.  

We also snagged a few yuzu black sesame donuts.  We got there at 11:30 and were the first ones on the line.  It was super flavorful and tangy.  Again, very good, but would I wait on another line of 30 folks?  I likely won't next time.

I had an absolutely phenomenal dinner the other night at Wildair - they do tend to get pretty busy, so definitely recommend making a reservation via Resy if you can. Everything was delicious and fresh, and I love that they incorporate seasonal ingredients to their ever changing menu. The clams were some of the best things I've ever had (such an interesting flavor profile), and the tartar was delicious as well. The waiter talked me into dessert, which was unreal!  Cannot recommend their panna cotta enough - they garnish it with this apple cider foam which I could easily chug straight from the bottle. It's slightly more causal than it's next door sister, Contra, but it's a similar experimental menu (actually prefer Wildair's).

A pretty bad incident occurred during our meal (hence my lowish rating), but management made it right afterwards, so I'm going not going to elaborate on it. Instead, I will focus on the food. 

My boyfriend and I came for dinner and tried:

+ Marinated mussels
+ Beef tartare 
+ Chicory and boquerones
+ Jerk shrimp skewers
+ Stuffed chicken wing 
+ Stuffed olives
+ Wildair tart
+ LES Paris brest

The highlights were the beef tartare and the desserts. Wish they had more of the highlights I had been looking forward to (like the fried squid), but everything we tried was tasty enough.

The food is beyond excellent and the reception at the door by the hostess, is also pleasant. The downside? Dour service by my waiter. I was literally the first person to enter the restaurant today evening and the server couldn't be bothered. If the service is so blasé with ONE customer, what would they do on a night with a full-house?! This was probably the first (and hopefully the last) time that i didn't bother leaving a tip. I left in under 30 minutes, vowing never to come back for a dine-in experience. Takeout...yes..

author.name: Naiyya S.
author.location: Lower East Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: Great wine bar with excellent service; our waiter offered extremely detailed and helpful descriptions of wines and all the food. He was also really great about some food allergies and how to order the stuff we wanted safely. The bread was SO GOOD, don't skip that. Also the radishes with butter, mmmmm.

This is a review for their menu back in early October 2021 (visited once in Sep 2021 as well)

Love their New American dishes, quite creative and complex. Chicken surely is my favorite piece, as is their tartare. Their beef tartare is an AMAZING take on a traditional dish. Love to see how they do innovative perspectives on traditional dishes. 

Desserts and wines are amazing too!

Popped in again last night for a glass of wine and dessert and was, unsurprisingly, blown away. 

The great atmosphere and relaxed vibe make it almost too easy and convenient to stop by for a quick, delicious glass of wine and a snack, and their food is regularly innovative and unique. 

Tried the new LES Paris Brest yesterday and I don't think I've had a better desert in recent memory. It's rich, to be sure, but also texturally interesting, with the walnut praline giving each creamy bite a unique, pop-rocks like crunch. Try it if you can.
I will be completely honest... I didn't even eat here. The hostess was rude enough too deter us before we threw away our money. Don't ask to see the menu or about availability. This will anger her.
Consistently delicious desserts and extensive natural wine list.  Staffs are friendly and knowledgeable.

I've stopped by several times at Wildair and they always have something new and inventive. I know they've developed cult status for their donuts (which are amazing) but I have also had their world class hot chicken sandwich and today an Asian inspired steak sandwich. Both showcase their ability to simple comfort foods and elevate them to the highest level. Spicy. Great balance with pickled veg. Really really good.

Small restaurant with lots of high tops. Drink menu is lots of wine with a few cocktails. Menu has a lot of random delicious dishes. I would recommend ordering at least 6-8 dishes to share between 2 people as portions are small. Delicious dessert and donuts if you are lucky to get your hands on some. 
4/5 because the service was pretty slow. None the less would probably go back.

I've been meaning to try the donuts at Wildair for some time and am glad that I did because oh they are amazing.  The problem with most cream filled donuts is that there's never enough cream but for Wildair donuts it's quite frankly the exact opposite.  The donut flavors change frequently and I tried the cookies n cream flavor which was delicious.  The only downside is the price but it's worth it IMHO.  The only recommendation I have is that they actually taste a lot better chilled than at room temperature, but this could also just be personal preference.  All in all worthy of a try, and I definitely plan on trying more flavors.

Wildair is up and running, and back to its awfully cramped and tight indoor seating. Even with a reservation, my party of two was led to a table sandwiched between two other parties - there was less than an inch between the tables and we would have practically formed a mega table.

Anyhow, I chose to sit outside since it was almost as miserably hot inside, and I wouldn't be privy to the conversations of the parties on either side of me.

The food and wine remains delicious as last time - I had the endives with boquerones, the beef tartare, the stuffed chicken wings, and the tomato bread. The endive salad was the best - I loved the salty fish along with the Nori crumbs on the endives. The stuffed chicken wings were good and reminded me of how southeast Asian wings might be barbecued, but they were noticing special.

The beef tartare looked rather grey when it appeared on my table, but it was well-seasoned. The tomato and miso bread crisps were excellent, even if the bread got a bit soggy by the dish's end.

Great natural wine options that's served at the right temperature, along with chill music. It's good for a date night - as long as you snag a table that isn't right smack in between other people.

Every weekend they offer donuts starting at noon. If you don't get here early enough chances are they will have already sold out. It's happened to me the very first time and it left a scar so deep I decided to never go back

...Until today! My barre class started at 12:15 so I had 15 mins to spare. It was very suspenseful at one point because it was 12:06 and I was still second or third in line, but I secured the donuts and made it to class.

The donut flavor today was chocolate chip. They also had a passionfruit eclair. I got both. The donut was phenomenal. It was well worth overcoming my fear of coming back and getting turned away again. The dough is where it's at. It's super fresh and soft. The filling isn't too sweet. The candied orange peel on top was interesting.

The eclair pastry itself is really good. Eggey, moist, and dense. The filling was vanilla bean and passion fruit. Also not too sweet or dominating.

If you happen to be around this place at noon on weekends and are craving some bangin donuts, definitely give this place a visit.
I didn't want to believe the hype. But believe it. Get the chicken sandwich. Get the breakfast sandwich. Get the donut.

I found this place to be just ok for the food. The baked goods are incredible but their signature chili beef sandwich with the dipping sauce fell flat for me due to lack of discernable heat or salt or even any elements of acid in the dish. What they do really well are the pastries and for that I will be back. But I felt disappointed for the sandwich because the bread was incredible.  The service was amazing and friendly which is also another great reason to return. Maybe they were having an off day.

I came solely for the tiramisu donut. I've waited in line before and they sold out the customer before me! Since this was my origin story, this time I got there 45 minutes before they opened at 12pm to ensure my donut lol. Totally worth the wait and the hype! If you're there by 11:35ish you should be able to get one. Definitely go! Can't wait to see what else they come up with.

I've gone back time and time again, it proves to be the best pastry I have had in nyc by far. I've had the apricot Crem brûlée donut, a cardamom cream filled donut, a strawberry shortcake eclair, passion fruit coconut donut, and each time it's such an incredible treat. How do they do it? Idk. They do it RIGHT though. I need to eventually have something other than their donuts and eclairs one day. Will check back when that time comes. The trick is, you have to get here a little before their opening time. Wait in line, it's worth it I promise.
I had the passionfruit eclair. This was light, fresh flavor and had plenty of the passionfruit filling. Looking forward to trying more from here!

Came here Saturday afternoon and of course their donuts were sold out. But then got the Chinese chili beef sandwich and jerk shrimp sandwich. Loved the Chinese chili beef, even though it came with a sauce but felt that the sandwich itself it's good enough. Jerk shrimp also taste pretty good but just a bit salty. Hopefully in the future I could manage to get to try their donuts

Absolutely delicious. Love the grilled jerk shrimp skewer, the badger flame beets with nectarines & yuzu, their Negronis, wine selection, shrimp burger, scallop crudo, duck rilettes, spicy tuna with tomatoes, fried chicken sandwich, unusual special donuts & creative seasonal veggies.  Good pop ups / collabs occasionally too.

I would say customer service was great. I got the veal tongue and tripe sandwich and while it was flavorful enough the sandwich was too soggy and made it difficult to enjoy. I feel like this is a dish if refined could actually be so much better to experience.

Their banoffee pie doughnut was freaking amazing! I was lucky to get one before they sold out and I'm soooo happy I did.

It's light and buttery with a delicious shaved topping. I've had a few amazing doughnuts in nyc and this one def tops the list. I hope they make this doughnut again!

Uhmmm been wanting to try this place but little nervous about the opposite reviews.

My experience was hit and miss. It's also my mistake chose to come here on the day before they closed for the Thanksgiving Weekend (well usually the leftover ingredients)

Steak Tartar - not good, not fresh, overly sauced probably to cover the not fresh meat..... ugh.

Fried Scallop - pretty good but also a bit salty, little heavy on the seasoning. There's fried sliced lemon which was pretty interesting and tasty.

Chopped Clam Flatbread - highlight of the night. It was very good, made up little of other disappointment. The clam was within the flatbread which was unexpected. Tasty and the chive/xo gave a touch of asian flavor. Something I would crave for it again!

Mezcal Negroni - for $15 it was a too premade, light and tiny glass of cocktail done after 3 sip.

I heard their wine are actually the choice to go, more unique selection.

Seriously the most innovative, delicious food. Definitely in my top 3 favorite restaurants in all of NYC and I don't say that lightly. Every time I go, I like to try one of everything on the menu and I've never tried anything I didn't like. Shrimp burgers are dynamite, the veal tongue and tripe is off the charts. CHEFS KISS

Undertrained and highly immature staff. This restaurant has definitely gone down hill since the opening. Staff is inappropriate, extremely condescending to customs, and makes guests feel very uncomfortable. Decent wine menu which is about the only saving grace at this point.

3.5 stars

Do I think Wildair is overpriced for what it's offering? Yes. Did I enjoy my meal here? Yes.

The wine I had was excellent, and the small plates all paired very well with the wine. They've really mastered the ideal wine bar experience here - good vibes paired with delicious food and easy drinking - which is admittedly not as easy to achieve as it sounds. And also unfortunately does not come cheap.

Covid note: They have both outdoor dining and indoor dining, and the indoor dining actually opens up fully onto the street so is pretty close to being outdoor dining (they have floor to ceiling doors that just open up). 

We tried:

Beef tartare - Enjoyable although I think I personally prefer a bit more texture in my beef tartare. This version is more smushed than I would have liked.

Fennel - Delicious and different. It's cold and garnished with kumquats which really add another flavor dimension.

Shrimp burger - I had initially dismissed this dish when I saw it on the menu, but so glad my friend suggested it, as it may have been my favorite bite of the night? The potato bun really pulls it all together and the shrimp is nice and springy and delicious.

Veal tongue and tripe - I wish this came in a smaller size because this dish was the one large plate we had and it felt a bit too much. It's surprisingly spicy and the tripe and beef tongue were cooked very well - soft and flavorful. 

Chocolate hazelnut tart - Excellent dessert to round out the meal. Hopefully you're a fan of hazelnut, because it's in full force here. I liked the salt flakes in there too. A smaller tart than I was expecting but actually works really well because it's so rich.

The Shrimp Burger and Bacon Roll are really fun. Not sure what kind of bread they use for the bacon roll but I'd like to live in it for a week. Definitely worth checking out. Oh..... I'm terrible with veggies and fruits but the salads were a nice little appetizer.

This review is for their Little Shrimp Burger (5/5) only as I have yet to try anything else, and hot damn, I've never had a shrimp burger before but this is a high bar to beat. It was so flavorful and well balanced that I nearly devoured it in a few minutes before my partner looked at it longingly and got the last few bites.

There is room to sit outside but I got takeout. Wait was about 10 min. The woman taking orders was super friendly.

Super friendly service and great quality food. However, $13.06 for such a little dessert is pretty crazy - even in NYC. I loved the textures and it tasted delicious, but especially the hazelnut ganache wasn't outstanding (I had similar toppings before). Anyways, if you have the money- go for it!

Contra and Wildair collaborated for a limited run 2-day Taiwanese/Northern Chinese dim sum take out menu. I ordered some dishes to pick up. I unfortunately caught a stomach bug and had to email Contrair for a refund, and they were INCREDIBLY responsive and prompt. I wanted to give them a shoutout because I know restaurants are innovating and trying to keep pace with what's happening in the world, and I really appreciated their great customer service. 
Hope they do more Taiwanese take out in the future.
good food that is pretty creative. place is pretty small. real great for a date. make a rez far in advance.

Good atmosphere, music and friendly staff.  Great wine selection and staff helps you find what you like.  We shared a bunch of small plates.  Gem lettuce, clams, calamari, maitake, grain salad.  Everything was interesting and worth trying, but nothing was great.  The table next to us ordered the porgy and claimed it was the best fish they ever ate.

Just an unremarkable little wine bar, you might think if you lack connoisseurship of LES wine bars. I do, and such was my thought at the outset of my visit. Sitting on high stools makes me feel like a wee child, and I was ready to pen a ruthless review (see: November 2013's critique of The Green Man). "Give me a booth or risk my ire," as I have been known to say. Yet I was coaxed off my high horse by a pleasant waitress and an approachable menu. She found us a bottle of sparkling red wine despite none being on the lengthy roster of beverages. We ordered the beef tartatre with smoked cheddar, the potato darphin (it's a latke) with uni, the little gem lettuce with pistachio, the bacon toast with pickled pineapple (reminded me of Dominos' world-renowned Hawaiian pizza), fried calamari with squid ink mayo, and the banana mille feuille with caramel. Sometimes you need a sweet after you've had your fill of savory plates. Do you agree? Leave a comment and I'll respond to the friendliest ones.

Very good ambience and food. The place is big on Natural wines, the server was very knowledgeable ajout the options and able to make good recommendation. 
The highlight for the food is the Milanese and the black Maitake. The Milanese is breaded perfectly and the Maitake is bursting wiith contrasting texture with the chicken skins.

I went here upon a recommendation from my friend that said the food and the service was great. He did mention that the wine list was going to be vast but that the service staff was very helpful to help you navigate towards what you wanted to drink. That did not turn out to be the case during my visit. Our waiter was slightly dismissive and we did mention that we were overwhelmed with the choices and he helped us find a bottle briefly, which was nice, but the rest of the service he provided us for that evening was awful. Our food came later than other people who had arrived before us. We had to follow up with him twice with out receiving any apology or explanation as to why our food was so delayed. When we finally got our food he didn't come to check in on us and we had to ask someone else to help us get a napkin and get some water. All the other staff members were lovely which I believe contribute to the good reviews but the man Who served us was quite terrible. One of the people in my party went back because the food is amazing and was served by the same man and continued to receive awful service from him. The food here is a GREAT, most of the staff that we encountered were quite lovely and the wine was great. I would definitely come back here hoping that he would not be my server again

Worth 5 stars for the LES Mess popcorn dessert. I haven't been that impressed by a dessert in a long time. We also got the little gem salad, crudo and bread. I know very little about wine but loved what I chose. 

Great for a date or casual catch up. Restaurant is tiny and it's hard to get a reservation but not impossible. 

Fun dining experience that we need more of in this city.
Over due review of Overrated restaurant with overly acidic, salty food and small portions. I guess people are are easily influenced by the hype.

I was very excited to try this place but regretted it after. So much hype here but the food didn't deliver for the price. I definitely had buyers remorse after and was a bit angry that I had spent so much on dinner without being satisfied. We had one of everything on the small plates with the beef tartar being the only standout. The wine list was massive, really wouldn't know where to start without suggestions. The wine we ordered was really good at $75, just pricey. We left spending over $200 and feeling very disappointed.

One of my favorite spots in Manhattan. Everything in the menu is delicious, but my favorites are the grain salad,  the maitake, and the whole fish is also delicious. For dessert, the hazelnut tart is marvelous! Amazing natural wine list. They also have kombucha. The staff, oh the staff...they are my favorite people!

What a treat! I dined here solo not too long ago when my partner was out of town for work. Since I was by myself it was easy to get a seat but it was pretty packed even though it was fairly early in the evening. I ordered a couple of plates and went with the staff's recommendations for wine. Both dishes I had was phenomenal and the wines were also excellent! I ended up chatting with my neighbor who was also dining solo and it was a lovely dinner. A little bit on the pricey side but the quality of the dishes and the fantastic range of wines both make it worth the price tag in my opinion. Perfect for an intimate dinner date or for anyone who's a wine geek of sorts. And what I loved was that the entire atmosphere and service was unpretentious and casual enough for anyone to feel comfortable. As a side note, I also very much enjoyed my dining experience at their sister restaurant Contra so if you like Wildair and haven't been, I highly recommend it.

I don't like to write negative reviews unless an experience was truly bad, and my experience at Wildair was truly bad. 

We had been told by several friends and bartenders to check out Wildair because we're huge fans of natural wine. We asked our waitress to recommend wine and she said that they were having a cider tasting. I said that I wasn't really in the mood for cider so I'd like to try the wine, and she said: "ok so you want the cider?" I repeated that I want to try the wine, and she asked if I wanted the wine WITH the cider. (like...WHAT IS HAPPENING RIGHT NOW?) She was either being super pushy about the cider or just completely absentminded. She sent over the cider guy (who was great) but never sent over my wine. When she asked what we wanted to order next she said, "oh you went with the cider" and I said, "yeah...because you never sent the wine!" and she didn't apologize or have a second of self-reflection.

We ordered bread and cheese, which is the only part of Wildair that I'd recommend.

We asked the waitress to recommend some wine to us again because we really didn't want any more cider. She picked out a glass of wine and when we asked for more information about the tasting notes she said: "I don't know, it's like fruity...but not fruity." And that's ALL she could say about it. Clearly this girl has absolutely no idea what she's talking about but we agreed to a couple of glasses anyways. The wine tasted like straight-up acetone and was the total opposite of what I was asking for. I honestly wouldn't have been mad if she had been able to explain what we were tasting, but without the context, it was like I was sipping on nail polish remover. For a $23 glass of wine, I was appalled. 

We decided to call this a loss and asked for the bill, and when a different server ran our card, he came back and said that he accidentally ran our card on someone else's bill and would refund us the $2 difference (what?). I was confused and asked why he couldn't just void the check and run our actual bill, and after a few moments of back and forth, he agreed to charge us for the appropriate bill. I legitimately felt like I was in the Twilight Zone.

To the Wildair team: this experience was laughably bad for a place that's so expensive and pretentious. The waitress with the rattail haircut was one of the worst servers I've ever had and completely ruined the experience for us. The weird part is that she was shadowed by a man for the first half and he definitely wasn't doing anything to help. I'm sure that your selection of food and drinks is wonderfully curated but without properly trained servers, it doesn't matter. I'm still angry that I spent $75 on this.

I had high expectations for this dining experience, perhaps too high. The food was just okay. Of the five things we ordered, the Maitake was the only dish to elicit a positive response. The quality of the food simply does not justify the price here.

The wine was the best part of the meal. The server was exceptionally in tune with all of the options (and there are a ton of options), and we loved his suggestion.

I went here a few nights ago with a group 6 people. The plates are all small and shareable. The wine list is extensive however it's difficult to find anything under $70. This service is fantastic. They're always there but never too intrusive. There's so many fun things about the space. The tables are all high tops with an old fashion school desk feel. 
As for the food:
PROS: 
Wagu (expensive but if you have a large group, it's worth the share! Excellent flavor and perfect for those craving a good piece of meat)
The mushroom salad with crisp chicken skin
The bread (you have to order it. Not complimentary)
The "Sicilian" sashimi

CONS
Between the 6 of us, we ordered nearly everything on the menu (aside from a couple entrees), plus 3 orders of bread and 3 desserts and we were all still hungry!
My recommendation is to try it out if you want some great flavors but to not go when you are starving!
I'd recommend it but I personally wouldn't go again. 
It was pricey and there are a lot of other restaurants worth trying!

This is the place you go to and leave saying "meh, it was aiight". 

Wildair in my opinion is a 3/5 star establishment. Place aside the excitement that it's Contra's next door younger sibling and let's focus on what the place offers at its $$$ price point. 

Ambience: Cool little LES restaurant. It's got the bar table seating vibe going and good energy inside. Except, I'm a stickler for good lighting. Good lighting sets the mood, and Wildair's white fluorescent lights just don't do it for me. My grandma's got these hooked up in her apartment in Hong Kong. Check the photo below -5/10

Service: Phenomenal. Friendly service from start to finish. Loved our server!! 10/10

Food: Other reviewers have overhyped it in my opinion. 

Spicy tuna over toast tastes like tomato sauce /tomatoes over toast. 

The fried squid tastes like the ones you'd get salt and pepper fried at a Chinese joint on Mott St.

And the signature dish!! Uni over potato darphin. It's actually just a salty hash brown with a scoop of uni on top. $26

I nearly cringed after they'd told me at 6:30pm that they were about to run out of the signature dish and I should reserve one immediately. Got me all excited for a sec. When I ate it, I was like .. wot? You were about to run out of these hash browns and uni? Not that special.. 

5/10

Verdict: Wildair tries very hard to be creative and the different guys on the block. I'd left with buyers remorse and depending on your expectations for food quality/ price, you may or may not too.

I visited Wildair as one of my farewell meals with a friend before my move out of NYC. We managed to snag some counter seats right by the kitchen, I think those are some of the best seats! Couldn't order as many dishes as we would have liked since there were only two of us, but here is what we got (and we were stuffed!!!):

Top Neck Clams, XO, Almond Milk $13
Not the best clams I've had, but it was more interesting with the almond milk added! Comes with 4.

Beef Tartare, smoked cheddar, horseradish, Brazil nuts $17
This was really good! Loved the massive amount of horseradish that they put on top.

Fried Soft Shell Crab, lemon, scallions $30
This was an insanely HUGE plate - definitely get your money's worth! This was done so well, perfectly deep fried and flavored. It also comes with some pieces of vegetables, watch out though, some of them can be lemon slices haha. Didn't love those.

Whole Porgy with Roti $38
Another humongous dish! This was also really good, fish was extremely tender. Loved the Roti that came with it too, I can eat plates of that just on its own :P

Almond Mille Feuille, fig $14
Nice ending to the night, mille feuille was nice and crispy (hate when I get these and it's soggy). Not too sweet, which I really appreciate!

Time to visit their sister restaurant, contra!

The best fine dining experience you can get in New York at this price point. Both Contra and Wildair excel in elevating the food without the pretentiousness to go with it. 

Maybe they are democratic socialists and value making good food available to more people rather than just the elite few. Or maybe they just love good food with good company. Whatever it is, it works.

We ordered everything on the menu except for the beef wagyu, which I've had there before and felt that, while good, not really something I $135-and-one-hour-wait need to have.

My personal favorite of the night was the Maitake, squash blossoms, stracciatella, chicken skin. The maitake mushrooms were a little taste of umami heaven. 

The other stars of the night were the
- Breakfast radishes, seaweed butter a.k.a. unexpected goodness! 
- "Sicilian sashimi", meyer lemon a.k.a. so fresh and so clean clean
- Crispy grain salad, heart of palm, tarragon a.k.a lick the plate and get every last grain
- Potato darphin, hokkaido uni, jalapeño a.k.a. I didn't think I liked uni until now (not me, someone else in our group said this)
- Spicy tuna on toast, tomato, sesame a.k.a. how can something so simple taste so good?

And the service, of course, was incredible. They were warm and so welcoming. 

Wildair has got to be one of my favorite restaurants in New York if not the favorite.

People in NY are flakey. Too many times I've been told the day of that the plans are cancelled. As the saying goes .. when one door opens, another one opens. This was true for my visit to Wildair, where a friend canceled dinner plans and I was able to join in on my coworkers resys.

The chefs of Wildair - Jeremiah Stone & Fabian von Hauske - come from 2018 Michelin star sister restaurant Contra. Wildair is super casual with all high top tables. The utensils and napkins are located under the table and it was very reminiscent of middle school desk.

Foodz:

Bread and olive oil - usually my favorite was just average and didn't taste like anything special to me

Top neck clams, XO, almond milk - loved the XO and the uniqueness from the almond milk - the clams were super fresh

"Sicilian sashimi", sorrento lemon - came with 4 types of fishes - simple dish yet realyl flavorful 

Beef tartare, smoked cheddar, horseradish, brazil nuts - 

Spicy tuna on toast, tomato, sesame

Fried Soft-shelled crab - Everyone's favorite dish of the night! It was perfectly fried with this delicious batter, the sauce was amazing

Dessertz:

Almond mille feuille, plum - my coworkers loved this dish - it was like a grown up smores

Chocolate hazelnut tart - my favorite dessert, chocolate was light and paired perfectly with the tart

"LES mess" panna cotta, peach granita - really refreshing dish, but my least favorite out of the three

Our waiter / sommelier poured us some great wines and we ordered a bottle of rose. Service was attentive the whole night. The restaurant can get loud and tables are super close to each other, so if you want an intimate dinner, this might not be the place.

One  of  the perks to dining alone is being able to squeeze into a single seat as a walk in. Tiny space, very crowded with people packed on the sidewalk hoping/waiting to get in. Service was good, not uber attentive which is understandable considering how packed they were and how tight the tables are to each other. I ordered quickly, asked for a tannic red wine and the server nailed it with the Andrea Cervini, Navel Rosso. It was just right. I knew I wanted the beef tartare to start and it did not disappoint. I was tempted to lick the plate but was so close to the woman next to me there was no way to make it happen without being seen. I asked the server what I should have as an entree and without hesitation she said "Whole porgy with roti, it's delicious." She was right. Full disclosure, I had no idea what that was when I ordered it. Head on fish and it was phenomenal. Texture, flavor, portion, you name it. It was exactly what I wanted yet had no idea going in. They asked if I wanted dessert but I could tell they needed the seat so I declined. Lucky me because 5 doors down there is a specialty Ice Cream Sandwich shop that hit the spot! All in all, a dinner win in New York. I will be back.
I came to Wildair twice in one weekend. While the wine list is awesome and the food is good, the meal was just waayyy overpriced for how hungry I felt afterwards.

Bread and olive oil (4.5 stars): small loaf of housemade sourdough with a crackly crust and light spongy interior. Olive oil was fresh and grassy

Beef tartare (4.5 stars): one of the best we've had in a while. Dressed with smoked cheddar shaved on top, which we would not have thought to pair

Maitake with stracciatella (5 stars): another wonderful and creative combo. Full of umami balanced by cream

Pork Milanese (5 stars): we never order this because we've only had cardboardy versions, but this was the exact opposite of that. Freshly battered and delicate, and very moist. Would order this again!

Panna cotta (5 stars): with strawberry granita. Very much in season, a light and balanced finish to the meal

Love their wine selection here! They have a very interesting selection with plenty of funky ones to choose from! Cocktails were also well crafted and just as good. Would love to come back to try the rest of the menu and more wine!

Service was very nice and attentive without being pushy. Also very knowledgeable about both food and wine. Walked in on a Thursday night at 7pm for 2 with no wait. Place is small and was pretty busy the entire time

It's been a few years since I went to wildair and glad I had a chance to go again this week. Wildair and contra are owned by the same person and both restaurants are consistently considered good. 

Wildair's menu changes seasonally and they have a great wine list. It's a little tough to go through the wine menu but the wait staff is really helpful choosing the right wine for your food. 

Food details below. 

Uni potato pancake - really interesting dish. The potato has texture that's extremely crispy and then soft on the inside. Uni makes the dish really creamy. 

Gem lettuce salad - you'll see this on most tables. They only have a few items that are vegetable forward. It's texturally nice and sharp from the vinegar. 

Lobster - one of the highlights. They pair it with two sauces and you eat it with a crepe-like. Delicious. 

Flakey biscuit - THE highlight. Can't describe how great these were. Flakey, buttery... don't skip on this. 

Chocolate hazelnut tart - rich and delicious. It's not too big so it's a perfect way to end the night.
Absolutely wonderful evening with amazing delicious dishes! The staff and chefs were so attentive. The food was ...perfect! Thank you!

author.name: Annie M.
author.location: Lower Garden District, New Orleans, LA

reviews.review: OMFG this place is special. I had dinner here a few nights ago on a date night with my hubs and it was magical. The service is so attentive - all of the suggestions were taken and we weren't disappointed. The food is BEYOND, and the atmosphere is casual despite the incredible food that is coming out of the kitchen.  BRAVO!

Meh

Service is really good
Wine list is grossly overpriced and nothing with age
Food was ok. Not great
Not a good place for a two need a big group to try lots. Of stuff
Wasn't really impressed by the food

Had the fried crab and it was very good. Breading was top notch and the lemon zest was on point. Also, the PB hazelnut tart was incredible. That really blew me away and surprised me how excellent it was. Finally the staff really impressed me with how they went out of their way to make me feel welcome after I told them I was visiting from SF. Would definitely go back.

The restaurant is simple, small but with a very cozy and lovely ambience. The staff is very friendly and helpful, listen to them because their tips are priceless.

The wine list is quite unique and difficult to navigate but I'm very glad that I trusted our server who after asking a few question paired the perfect wine with our meal. They have some gems on that wine list.

Let's talk food. The plates ARE small but come on, look at the prices, they are supposed to be more tapas style and be shared. Order plenty because everything I put in my mouth was just superb. 

Small dishes that look simple on paper deliver on flavor and complexity. The menu is not extensive but everything was so carefully balanced and delicious that it is impossible not to love. For example the addition of smoked cheddar cheese on a beef tartare is just the most incredible thing I've ever tasted.

If you are an always very hungry person (like me) just order more, the whole menu if needed, you won't regret or be hungry, simple as that! The prices allow you to and everything is delicious!

I've seen some commenters complaining about being hungry, DON'T believe them! This is the cheap type of people that think "bread should be free", like they could walk into a bakery and get whatever they want. Want "a deal" and be stuffed for 20 dollars? You belong at Applebee's! This place is only for the ones looking for quality.

IF you want to splurge on a top quality special treat for a special occasion (or not, just to be a happy diner), are a very hungry couple (or group) and are willing to pay for quality you MUST order the wagyu beef.  It's expensive, but be aware it's a top quality large piece of wagyu beef! It will feed 2 very "very hungry" or 3 "reasonably hungry" people. The beef is so damn good, rich and worth every penny. If you can afford it please treat your tastebuds to this!

Don't you dare not order dessert, they are delicious. The passion fruit mille feuille is out of this world!

At long last, I made it to Wildair for dinner the other night and it was well worth the wait. Their food and drink, the atmosphere, and the service are all I look for in a New York restaurant in 2019.

I will lead off by speaking to the awesome wine list here. Since only two in my party of four were drinking, we requested wines that were available by the glass. The server was happy to oblige with suggestions to pair well with the food - an Italian orange and a Mexican red (!). The Mexican red was not listed on the wine list, but it was one of the best glasses I have had in some time (Bichi Listan 2017).

To make things simple for ourselves, we ordered the first ten main plates listed on the menu, skipping the $39 lobster and $140 steak. I cannot recommend this approach more highly if you are coming in a group of four or more.

FOOD

Must gets (the menu changes seasonally, but if you spot these, order them and ask questions later):

-Sunday biscuits (the butter this is served with is ridiculously creamy as are the biscuits themselves, all for $6)
-Boudin noir with fig and spicy onions (even those that are averse to blood sausage need to try this)
-Fried squid (served with a heavenly squid ink mayo and includes fried lemons and leeks too!)
-Potato darphin with Maine uni and jalapeno (like a French latke but better, probably because of the uni)
-Black maitake, stracciatella, chicken skin, and tomatillo (mushrooms are always a win in my book, but this is one of the best dishes starring mushrooms I have had)

Also very good were the beef tartare with smoked cheddar, Sicilian sashimi, little gem lettuce with pistachio, crispy grain salad, and pork milanese. Only the confit bacon toast was a bit disappointing as the pickled pineapple overpowered the dish.

And of course, we wrapped up the night with a coupled desserts, those being a passion fruit and caramel mille feuille and a coconut panna cotta with blood orange granita.

What really sets Wildair apart is the atmosphere, with high tops squeezing 30-40 people into the equivalent of an LES apartment. However, this makes for a lively and communal atmosphere where people are obliged to peek over at a neighbor's table and inquire what plates to order. When you step through Wildair's doors, it really does feel like you have entered into a community dining room.

This is a cute spot in Lower East Side across the street from Russ and Daughter's Cafe. You sit at high tops that are reminiscent of school desks. They have an open kitchen as well. 

We ordered the potato darphin with Maine uni, beef tartare, black maitake, confit bacon toast, and pork milanese. Overall the dishes were all very good. The only item that was only okay was the pork. 

Service could be better however. They forgot my drink and didn't remember until I reminded them 20 minutes later. They also had to ask me for my order again. I'm always rather annoyed when waitstaff try to impress by remembering orders. I'm more impressed when you write it down and get my order right the first time around. 

But all that said, the food was good and the service wasn't horrible. I'd come back to give it another chance.
This place was cute and nice. Their uni on potato was good and unexpected. They have a great natural wine list. Their little neck with coconut milk was also superb.

This is one of those places where I rarely say anything negative. The food was overrated. It was a recommendation from chef Justin Yu from Theodore Rex in Houston, so he's going to have to take some responsibility as well. Theodore Rex is a 5 star establishment. I ordered at Wildair, I guess cause the air is gassy, the clams, the off menu crudo, and the fried calamari and vegetables with squid ink. The clams were the highlight, as the chef was able to balance the brine and showcase it with the almond milk, xo, and other flavors. However, the crudo was 50pct fresh. The fish had a low quality taste to them, although they were cut nicely. There was not much garlic chili flavor as well, which a bit more spice would have improved the dish. The calamari was nothing special except it was gluten free having been fried in potato and corn starch. The squid was whatever and the vegetables were whatever. Whatever the sauce was, it was a schtick of just lemon juice in squid ink. I have a feeling I just ordered the wrong items, or the restaurant was having an off night.

I came to Wildair for my birthday a few weeks ago. It was fun experience with a really well curated menu. A big part of the experience for me was their organic wine options. It was fun to pair with our dishes as they came out.

Wildair is bar height seating, and we were lucky enough to sit right in front of the kitchen. I love open kitchens and watch the chefs prep dishes to send out.

We ordered the clams, fresh bread,green goddess salad, beef tartare, bacon on toast, fried squid with black mayo, pork Milanese, and my favorite..... the panna cotta with blood orange granita. 

Honestly, everything was delicious and worth ordering! I especially loved the bacon on toast, squid, and Milanese.

But please, don't leave without trying that panna cotta.

DELICIOUS food, but NOT the place to go if you are  HUNGRY. The portions are super small. With that warning the food was amazing and the waitress was very good at explaining what everything was. It was tapas style and I will name everything we had in order according to how yummy it was....the crispy grain salad (wow!), the lobster crepe, the pork Milanese, a bacon toast, the hazelnut chocolate tart, cheese platter with biscuits, a mushroom dish (with what seemed to be polenta on the bottom). Wine list was also very good!

I LOOOOVE WildAir.
The food is delicious, - my fav combo is their bread with radishes and seaweed butter (I did notice the bread is the freshest on Tuesdays ;), 
Tartar is to die for! Squash blossom, stracciatella, chicken skin surprised me in a VERY good way. Desserts are masterpieces per usual. 
Servers are always chill and knowledgeable about their interesting wine list.
Chairs are tough to get in and out of, but what a small price to pay for such a great experience every single time.

This was our first dining choice on a recent trip to NYC due to the great reviews Wildair had. Being from Portland, OR I was interested to see how PDX measured up to NY. 

I wasn't as impressed as I'd hoped to be. 

We started off great. The host accommodated a change in reservation due to a late flight and they were very polite. 

The wine by the glass was limited and I didn't find a selection I liked. 

Standouts for us: the fresh bread and olive oil and the oysters. 

The fried calamari had way too much breading on it and very little calamari and vegetables. In fact, the diners next to us actually peeled off all their breading and ate the minimal amount left. 

The black maitake dish was good and flavorful, more like I expected, but the portion was small. 

The beef tartare wasn't to our taste, we prefer classic, but it seems many people like it. 

Our waitress could barely smile. We were never asked about how our meal was and when we asked about plate suggestions, her comment was "everything is great", there was no further questions about what our tastes might be. 

Therefore, a bit of underwhelming  experience.

A good go-to casual yet LES hip foodie place to try.

Venue (4/5) casual, hipster venue.  This place has communal high table seating so don't expect privacy.  Good for small groups or dates.  
Tip: The tables have silverware in the table 

Food (4/5)
Steak tartar (5/5) a great balance of cheese, raw steak and sauces.  My friend which has a dairy sensitivity tasted this dish and took a couple other bites after.  I loved this dish.

Gem lettuce (3/5) good, but a bit small for the price tag

Pork Milanese (4/5) good and a generous portion

Fried squid (2/5) pass on this.  Pretty bland.

Skin contact wine (3/5) interesting the one we tried tasted like a blend of beer, kambucha and white wine

Service (4/5) good

One of the best meals and dining experiences I've had in ages. We were seated at the kitchen counter, as if there's ever a better seat. The restaurant is small and vibrant, so any seat works. We started with drinks. Small, but impactful beer and wine list. Started with oysters. So fresh and buttery. Then moved to the clams. Wow, what an amazing flavor burst. Would have ordered more but we already ordered most of the menu. Then came the uni on latke. I didn't want this to end. And as our "main" dish, the chicken cutlet. This is as good as a cutlet gets, tenderized, seasoned, breaded and fried to perfection. I could have eaten 5 of these! The service was fantastic and the atmosphere is so lively. I'll def be back soon. Def next time I'm in NY!

4.5 stars - loved almost everything I ordered. here were some standouts, although the menu is constantly changing so these dishes may not be available on the day you decide to go:

top neck clams with XO sauce - unexpected pairing, raw briny clams with a dried scallop/Chinese sausage sauce. VERY GOOD

fried softshell crab with preserved lemons doused with bay seasoning- the batter on this was delicious - chewy and airy and extremely flavorful all at once? softshell crab was tender and flaky and sweet. 

scallop crudo and meyer lemon - sweet, citrusy, buttery scallops in a creamy dressing. refreshing and light and zesty

beef tartare with smoked cheddar, brazil nuts and and horseradish - really balanced, nutty, spicy, tingly. my favorite rendition of beef tartare to date.

Panna cotta with pluot granita - sprinkled with a dash salted caramelized milk crumbles - seriously mindblowingly good. words cannot describe. 

chocolate hazlenut tart - pure silky decadence.

Best restaurant in NYC and I tried 100 in one year!
Very interesting taste fireworks, cool vibes, not too expensive, excellent wine choice, nice service personel

Wildair is a trend-setting Lower East Side restaurant specializing in post-modern small plates and natural wines. Its sister restaurant Contra a couple doors down shares a similar ethos, but whereas their tasting menu approach leads you gently (and affordably) through Jeremiah Stone and Fabian Von Hauske's vision, Wildair's a-la-carte ordering throws you right in.

This restaurant has been perennially popular, and though some reservations are available through reserve, you're best off putting your name in for one of the many walk-in slots. We were told an hour wait around 8 on a Friday night and it ended up being more like 45.

Let's start with a drink. There are a handful of cocktails and aperitifs on offer, but you'll find no by-the-glass wine or beer offerings. Instead, there's a daunting bottle list of natural wines, with the lower end in the $60s and most ringing in at $80-120 if I recall correctly. Best of luck finding what you're looking for; they've got some funky stuff going on, with many unusual grapes and small producers. Servers are knowledgeable about the list and can guide you, and our Slovenian white was certainly out of our wheelhouse but not bad for cooling off in the heat.

We weren't starving and weren't quite sure what to expect from portions, so we went for three savory dishes. Scallop crudo ($16) was completely forgettable. Mussels with endive ($18) rang more bells for me, both visually and texturally, but the mussels were completely buried in the mass of crunch and sauce.

Our favorite dish by a country mile was the potato darphin with uni ($29). You have never had such potatoes... the crispy, golden brown exterior, the delicate interior weave of potato, with the soft uni acting as a briny butter. Add the bits of pickly jalapeno and you have perfection. A brilliant dish, though it's really just a few bites.

Panna cotta ($10), topped with a simple strawberry granita and a crumble, was well-calibrated and a nice way to end the meal. However, we still felt a little light going home.

The meal rang in around $90 a person after tax and tip, though much of that owed to the wine. I'm sure they have good reasons not to offer a by-the-glass program, but it's not ideal to have to commit to a bottle as a pair in terms of the bill, personal tastes, and drinking capacity. 

The decor is sophisticatedly minimalist. It feels like a happening place to be, but it was a bit too noisy for us. Our visit was in early June and the combined heat of the room and the open kitchen was overwhelming. Seating can be rather tight, and most, if not all, seating is low-backed high stools.

Service is great; calmly capable and attentive despite a busy room. They have this way of talking with you that's slightly conspiratorial; you wish that they were your slightly-too-cool friend from college who still texts you to catch up. Pacing was relaxed. A well-heeled and artsy-looking clientele.

Overall, I think the prices are pretty high and the experience, despite the service, was intimidating, and I say this as someone who typically feels confident dining out. Navigating the inscrutable wine list as well as trying to chart a course through the food wasn't a challenge I relished. If you must try Stone and Von Hauske's cuisine, I think Contra is a far better introduction.
Honestly one of the best dinners I've had in NYC including the food, service and ambiance.

One of the most expensive meal I ever had! 
I used to go to Wildair when it opened and loved it so much. Few weeks ago, I went back there with my friend and was surprised to see the place half empty... (used to be at least an hour wait for a sit) now I understand why... 
service super nice, great wine, but the food... it was OK, but not crazy, and sooooo small! We had three plates to share, couple glasses of wine each, the cost was $200!!!! For tiny portions of OK food. Had dinner when I got back home.
Won't go back.

A cold March evening. Finally, an open reservation on Reserve for 2 people at a decent time.

We got seated right away, right in the middle of an essentially communal wine bar table. Definitely cramped, but that's just how it is in LES, haha.

What we got:
- Bread and olive oil (duh)
- Topneck clams
- Mussels with endive and smoked egg yolk
- Potato darphin with uni
- Tête de cochon on toast
- Beef tartare
- Fried squid with black ink aioli
- Pork milanese with Meyer lemon
- Chocolate Tart

We enjoyed every dish, but I will say that the small plates were much more hard-hitting with the flavors than the large plates (squid and pork milanese). That isn't to say the large plates were bad, maybe just not quite as exciting. Chocolate tart was very good, and a perfect ending to the meal.

Service was a little slow to begin with, and they took awhile in between courses, but began to pick it up as the night went on. Prices are reasonable for the area, but as the wine and spirits list is very extensive, you may find yourself wanting to try a bunch of different beverages.

Definitely worth a try if you have never been.

A friend recommended we try Wildair this weekend and we both liked it quite a bit. The menu was creative and diverse, and the wine selection was wonderful. The new American style reminded me of one of my favorites from home. We ordered several small plates and liked them all. I enjoyed the wine I had, maybe partly because the label was a Ghostbusters reference. The wall seating was a little cramped; try to get a middle table instead if you can!

Went for my birthday dinner as had heard great things. The waitress was incredibly too cool and made us feel like were less of human beings because we did not know what everything was on the pretentious menu. It was good food so it's a real shame the staff make you feel like you're the uncool kid in school.

Organic wine. Delectable food. The clams with the xo and almond broth were to die for. And so were the squid. Salivating as I type this. The wine we had was simply superb. You won't get full in this place without breaking the bank but you can't go wrong with it.

The place is super trendy. Posh. Crowded. Small. Boutique. We got there around 9pm and put our name down. Walked around the area a bit and didn't wait long once returning to the restaurant. Our waiter was a little aloof. Like just very chill pace, which was fine for the most part but also had no sense of urgency when it was needed.  In any case, it didn't take away from our experience. We tried 6 different things between the 3 of us. The plates are small and expensive. Expect about $50 pp to feel satiated.  I would definitely recommend trying the beef tartare. It was wonderful. And the panna cotta was amazing. There was a weird Grenada that I wasn't expecting in it (blood orange) but it paired well with the creamy. Definitely good food. Unique. Wasn't the best of anything I've ever had, but it was good.

wine was the highligjt, as was dessert and tbe steam tartare. grain salad was good, endive mussels too salty and ricotta potato salad mediocre. expected more from the inventive list, but still glad i went. wine was delicious- check my photo

We went bc it was recommend to us. The place is VERY small and VERY squished. The very small tables are literally butted up against each other so if you weigh more than 150 pounds you will be uncomfortable at best.
We sat at the counter that looks directly into the kitchen, so we got to see all the dishes being prepped. The waitress came and asked if we wanted a cocktail. I asked what they had for vodka. NO VODKA. NO RUM. NO MARTINIS. ALL they had was one tequila drink and one Gin drink, wine and a COUPLE beers... so if you like a couple cocktails before dinner... Like most people do, don't bother going.  The main dinner menu had 4 choices and NO specials. One of the choices is a steak for two that costs $108.00.  I watched the chef making this pricey hunk of meat on a flat top...no grill. After the steak was finished cooking, he put it aside to rest. When it was time to cut it up, he cut an inch and a half off each end and put it aside. Everyone knows the BEST PARTS are the end tips!!! Yeah, he saved those for himself. He plated the steak, put the potatoes on the side and drizzled them with something and then handed the plate off to the server. At this point I see him cut up the steak he saved and enjoyed it all for himself. If I am asked to pay $108.00 for a steak, I want all of it... Especially the best parts!!! 
Not worth the prices you will be charged!!!

I don't know why this place doesn't have a michelin star as well as their sister restaurant next door?  I love the ambiance in here. It literally screams New York. Unique dishes, a party of four could order every item on the menu and be able to taste all the diverse flavors there short menu has to offer. Great service on top of that. Each dish is a conversation. It's hard for me to find an ingredient I haven't tasted to seen bring cooked differently but these guys have that unf.

Cons:
You will leave hungry or poor. Don't or come early if you're a big group. 

Pros:
You're eating at one of the best restaurants in the city. Reservations (not sure if you can make any?) are a must if you're more than 2, but there is usually counter space that's almost always up for grabs for walk ins.

Each dish is deceptively simple. Reading the menu you'll think to yourself, "I can probably make this myself" But the truth is there is SO much prep and technique and fresh produce that go into the 3/4 ingredients that no honey you probably can't. 

It seriously, seriously is soOoOo unreal how good any vegetable tastes here. Their wine selection is also extensive and top notch. I always end up getting a bottle here.

My favorites:
- Clams with XO sauce (!!!)
- Pork Milanese (most filling thing on the menu aside from the $108 wagyu steak...)
- Sweet Potato, ricotta, and herb salad (o m g)
- bread and olive oil (not sure what they did to the oil but w o w)

Scallop crudo plate, persimmon dish, and beef tartare were all perfection. They maintained a delicate balance of the natural flavor with unique spices/preparations. Also, super fun and interesting wine list, including a bunch of pet nats, if you want some quirky bubbles.
Good wine selection. Salad wedge great. Desert cheese thing. Great dte staff. More pricey than youd expect. Tight seating.

Small but vibrant restaurant. Overall food was good. But uni was not that fresh.....
Disappointed with the uni dish.

Nice dinner spot! Definitely got the trendy vibe going with the low hanging old school light bulbs, and space efficient with a lot of high tables packed into a small space.
