THE WAIT: We got there at about 5:55pm on a Friday and were second in line (they open at 6pm). The place had filled up by about 6:30 or 6:45pm. 

COST: $44.74 total (including tax/tip) for 2 starters, 4 medium dishes, 1 dessert, split 3 ways. 

THE SERVICE: Our server, Jacob N, memorized our order. Then the wrong salad (Little Gem) was brought out. We said it wasn't ours, and Jacob came over and seemed to disbelieve that we ordered the Crispy Grain Salad, but that had been his strongest recommendation (plus, all 3 of us remember ordering it). They did finally bring out the Crispy Grain, but it came out way later than the rest of our food. 

MUST-HAVES: Littleneck Clams!

THE FOOD:
* Bread ($4) - 4 stars
We were curious that they were charging for bread, & it didn't disappoint. It was soft & dense, with a thick, crunchy crust.

* Littleneck Clams ($12) - 4.5 stars
Fantastic, everyone loved this! Very fresh & great flavor.

* Potato darphin, uni ($23) - 3.5 stars
The uni was good, but this wasn't the best pairing with a potato pancake. The two parts would have been better on their own.

* Crispy grain salad ($16) - 3.5 stars
The grains add some nice texture, but this wasn't as amazing as our server made it out to be. 

* Spicy tuna toast ($20) - 4 stars
Really nice, the fresh tomatoes really enhanced the tuna!

* Fried shrimp ($21) - 3 stars
Just not for me - the breading was a little soft, and there was too much lemon flavor in the shrimp. 

* Panna cotta, green apple granita ($8) - 3.5
The panda cotta was silky soft, the granita a unique addition.

Truly a stunning and memorable experience. 

I was visiting from out of town and heard from some of the wine professionals back at home that this was a must-visit. I can see why. 

I'll save the full play-by-play of our evening, but rest assured by the end of the night, we were chatting and laughing with total strangers sitting next to us and were completely stuffed to the gills with amazing food and wine. Here are the things you should know:

1. No reservations. So get here early, or be prepared to put your name on the list and come back much later.
2. Communal dining. Small chairs and aluminum counters are a tight squeeze, but it adds to the charm. 
3. Natural wines. This means minimal intervention. The wines on the list range from sweet and fizzy to funky and confrontational. You won't win any friends by saying the wine is "off" or "sour" (because that's pretty much what it's supposed to be), so come in with an open mind. 
4. Eat it. All. Eat all the things. The menu changes, and one night's showstopper (my friend said the potato and uni dish was heavenly) may not be there the next night! Our top dish was the simple-sounding mixed grain. Amazing. 

I'm jealous of you New Yorkers getting all this great food, but when you see great food reaching new heights like this, I have hope for the future.

I've been to Wildair twice. The first time, we had the most wonderful time: great service, excellent wines, and delicious food. Unfortunately, coming back on a Friday night may have been a bad idea. The food was good, but the service was terrible. Waiting unnecessarily for a table that's been ready for 10 minutes, having the tail end of a magnum dumped into my glass ($15), or waiting an ungodly amount of time for food that was at time overcooked is unfortunate. I like casual restaurants, but when I spend close to a hundred dollars per person on a meal, I still expect some professionalism. Wildair; please get your act together!

We love natural wine, and they have a huge and excellent selection here. Unlike other wine bars, the food actually trumps the wine. Items that read like bistro staples are in actuality gastronomy delights.

An umami-rich beef tartare with smoked cheddar and chestnuts adds some smoke and crunch. A rotating ceviche served in a shallow bowl is fresh and light, recently sliced scallops with some avocado and slivers of ripe jalapeño hidden in a thin layer cold, frothy broth tasting of low tide. A simple plate of fried shrimp turns into a party with deep fried lemon slices passing VooDoo potato chips as my new favorite fat snack.  The most outrageous, jump out of your seat and throw your hands in the air dish was nduja and pig face on a crostini. It's off the menu now. Ask for it anyways. If not go for the radishes and squash blossoms with straciatella. Just as good but much lighter. 

By going lighter, you should have room for the bread, which helps soak up some of the dishes if you don't attempt to fill your fat mouth a whole loaf as a chaser to the shot cup of salted butter, and the desserts. Oh the desserts. The chocolate hazelnut tart has ruined many candy bars for me while the Panna Cotta is a reminder that a yogurt parfait doesn't have to suck. 

Do not pass go, this place is killer and while it may ruin a few other restaurants for you, you can always pop in for a a glass of skin contact wine and a snack before you join the drunken masses on the Lower East Side. However, if you're anything like me, you'll struggle not to have a full meal here, likely just how they drew it up. Easily my favorite restaurant in New York City.

I was really impressed with Wildair. My friend and I came here on a Friday night (they don't accept reservations ahead of time) and we waited about 20 minutes for a spot. I loved the atmosphere and feel of the restaurant. It's a small place in an unassuming location, but very homey and welcoming. We were really pleased with the service as well.

We ordered:

1) bread with olive oil
2) half dozen oysters
3) beef tartare
4) spicy tuna toast
5) pork milanese 
6) chocolate tart

We enjoyed each dish, and I especially liked the pork milanese and the bread with olive oil. I'm a big fan of the "less is more" concept, and I think most of the dishes at Wildair fall into this category. They have a good thing going on

Heard about this place through the Grape Nation Podcast for their stellar wine program, so I knew it was going to be a great place to drink my favorites, which are Pet'Nats, but when I took a look at the food menu...mmmmmmm...I wasn't as thrilled as I was with their wine. 

I truly detest drinking on an empty stomach, and worse yet a restaurant with a beautiful wine menu and barely any food. This restaurant only has 18 items on the food menu, and thankfully, every single one of the items we ordered were delicious! 

We ordered...
1) their bread and olive oil. Seriously, the best sourdough I've ever had. Dense, hearty, fluffy, fragrant, fresh and with olive oil, it was fabulous. 
2) squash blossoms with stracciatella and chicken skin. As soon as I saw the chicken skin, I knew I had to order it! Squash blossoms are a soft edible flower which was made even softer and wetter with the stracciatella cheese, but the crispy, salty chicken skin gave it the perfect contrasting element to this dish.
3) the beef tartare, cheddar, horseradish, brazil nuts which wasn't ordered by me. My partner said he wasn't thrilled with this tartare. Nothing particularly special. I don't eat raw foods unless it's summer time which is why I was a bit disappointed with the veggies on their menu. 
4) the pork milanese, gribiche and mustard greens. Sizable. Very sizable. I could barely finish I was so full. Seriously, you can never go wrong with breaded pork cutlet.
It's great to sit in front of the open kitchen where you can see all the action. Food is delicious but not much of a drink selection

I love restaurants that serve you fancy food and has casual vibes. Although many can say that the food wasn't fancy, I thought the plating was fancy and by the look of portion to cost, it's pretty fancy. Yet you don't have to make reservations 30 days in advance. Reservations are not allowed but if you go early enough to put your name down, you could probably get seated by 8pm on Friday night. They seat larger groups first. Bummer, as we were only a couple. 

We each had a glass of wine and shared two dishes. The Spicy Tuna toast is to die for. Imagine Poké meets Italy meets New York on a plate. If it was $20 for a toast, I would've probably ordered 4 more. That's how good it was. We also had the beef tartare and that was bangin'. Wish we ordered a side of bread with it but that would've been too filling. 

Lastly we saw panna cotta on the menu and we just had to get it. I can't ever pass on panna cotta. This one was unique. There was pineapple granita on top of the panna cotta, without it there would've been a lack of sweetness. The panna cotta itself was smooth but had less structure. It was more of a pudding in a cup. 

Totally recommend this for a small group dinner or even date night but be prepared to wait. The hostess will call you when your table is up. We waited an hour.

This place is so good.  It is no-reservation and a super small space so come preparing to entertain yourself while you wait for them to text you that your table is available (no room to wait at the restaurant).  Inside they have definitely gotten creative with fitting a lot people in a small space so be prepared to sit very close to other diners.  We ordered the tartare, little gem, the stracciatella, the tuna with nudja and the fried shrimp.   Everything was really great with exception of the tartare with while easy wasn't anything special.  The tuna with nudge was particularly  create and good and I really liked that the friend shrimp were whole head-on shrimp (yummmm).  Aside from the great food both the waitress and the hostess were lovely and really friendly and the service was quick and well paced. I  would highly recommend going with four people so you can order the whole menu to try everything out.
One of my favorite meals in the city. Nearly everything we had was excellent, and a great mezcal negroni to finish.
Everything is of the finest quality. The wine list, for me, was a little hard to navigate but they are there to help. Plan a is getting the steak for two, plan b is sampling many items. Both win.
Hello Paria! The kind of restaurant all should be. So relaxed, so good, so everything. Whatever you do don't miss on the dessert

Stellar food. Simple dishes expertly executed with fresh ingredients bristling in flavor.  Had the best swordfish I've ever had. Plates range in sizes depending on the contents but ordering one from each of the 3 sections of the menu was a satisfying meal.

These guys killed it... food was killer our waiter Micheal paired a glass with each course. Get the uni, shrimp toast... actually everything . Thanks so much for a great dinner on my day off. Such good food and wine

from the service to the food, everything was pretty underwhelming. maybe i was expecting too much? fried shrimp was so over battered you couldn't even find the shrimp in the batter. i removed the batter off one of the shrimps and the shrimp was 1.5 inches long with the head on- maybe that's why i could taste only batter, because the shrimp was nearly non-existent? xo clams didn't taste briny or bright... just fishy. scallops were sweet but the avocado mess it was covered in was oxidized to hell. very bitter hokkaido uni with a thick piece of basically hash brown that completely overwhelmed the otherwise bad uni because it was so well-cooked (which was great but i didn't come here to pay $28 for a potato pancake). so so so disappointed. hoping this was an off-night but it was sat night. no wait at 8pm though, and the restaurant was half empty by 9:30pm, come at your own risk.

Everyone is really friendly and accomodating - a pleasant surprise at a trendy, small downtown spot.  The cost definitely adds up, but I should say we really ordered just about everything on the menu.  I had read a bunch about the menu, and in my opinion, the must-haves:

pork milanese
oysters
fried shrimp

The fois gras and the uni were both "eh".  Beef tartare, radishes, scallop crudo were all fine but not standout.  The wine list and cocktails didn't feel particularly exciting either.

When I finally visited Wildair, I have to admit, the menu seemed a bit underwhelming.

I recall sitting there thinking, is this Fried calamari really supposed to be the "main event"? It all seemed very... tame. 

Well, I'm happy to say that this is indeed the best fried calamari on the planet. Seriously. 

Everything they served was great. Exceptional bites accompanied by an excellent wine list and good cocktails. But that Calamari... (never thought I'd be this excited over fried calamari again) And the perfectly fried lemons... and the squid ink aioli....  
I mean there's just not much else to say. if you have the best of something, in a city with as much good food as New York, you get at least the four stars.

The entire staff there is so gracious and very pleasant.. Not an hint of douchbaggery.. That is really one thing we found, just on top of amazing food, the service was lovely, the room crowded but warm, it is really a wonderful place.

Several small plates of beautiful food are being produced out of this tiny kitchen.. They have a lovely wine list and crack several magnums for their by the glass program.. I usually order bottles of wine but, this place, you are better off trying a bunch of different wines by the glass. 

The steak tartar is phenomenal..The steak chopped perfectly into chewy pieces, covered with smoked cheddar and grated horseraddish, I was in love. We had this fried potato cake topped with a very large helping of uni.. This too was really a thing of beauty.. Next up were these raw clams topped with cream and some Chinese flavoring.. This too was among my most recent favorite bites of food.

They have these two very exciting salads too.. Little gem covered in with dill and lemon and pistachio dressing.. I could literally eat this salad every day and be happy.. They also have a crispy grain salad with hearts of palm and tarragon.. Yah, i was so down with this.. 

The place gets crowded so, I would suggest after 9:30.. Put your name down and grab a drink at one of the many bars dotting the surrounding streets.. 

The vibe is welcoming and  busy and warm and the food is among the most exciting around. Truly worth a visit.

Incredible food but very pricey. Crunch salad.... not sure what is in it which makes it so good but it is awesome! Waitress had brilliant knowledge of the wine list as well. Overall great place for nibbles and a drink but a by too expensive to spend much longer there.

Service that is bad enough to effect your meal. The kind of place where you feel you're being discouraged to ask questions because clearly you should already know the answer. The food was solid but there are too many spots in town where the staff try to make you feel welcome to return to one where they just can't be bothered to provide a basic standard of service.

Why am I so late to this party? 

I met my Bumble date for a "drink" at 6pm, Friday night, as the restaurant opened. It's not a bad idea to get there at weird times as Wildair doesn't take reservations so think early, or on Tuesday, for example. There were a handful of people waiting so we were seated without a wait and who isn't into that? I loved the small, well-thought out space, low-key vibe, and especially the clever tables with setups (napkins, cutlery) neatly tucked away into cubbies below the table tops, and the base structure which functions like a stowaway for bags, tech, jackets, etc. Wildair has floor to ceiling glass walls/windows, some of which open, as was the case, last night. Also: the "bar" seating directly in front of their kitchen makes for great entertainment, should you be into that sort of kitchen experience immersion. Next time, for me, for sure. 

I know that Wildair is known for its fabulous pet'nat wines but it was the first hot-as-hell-Friday of the season so we had cocktails: the Vago Mezcal Espadin & Negroni and the Vergano, Americano Spritz. I've had Campari. And I've had Mezcal. But I've never had them together. Not even kidding when I say this is the cocktail that I've been looking for my entire life. We had a few of each. 

My date decisively ordered bread and oil and 1/2 a dozen oysters. Sort of like an Old-Italian-Master snack. I was impressed. They serve their oysters as I like: with lemon. A mignonette was asked for and it appeared but honestly, the oysters were lovely in their naked state. I ordered the littleneck clams with XO and almond "broth"--these were ethereal. Lightly poached clams, chilled, in an almond milk (don't think smoothies or granola, folks), XO (that crazy delicious 1980s Hong Kong Cantonese condiment made of roughly chopped dried seafoods, including scallops, dried fish and shrimp, and subsequently cooked with chili peppers, onions, and garlic--sometimes even ham) and a bit of feathery, teeny tiny seaweed with bulbs. Gorgeous. And Delicious. The date agreed, even tho his bivalve preference doesn't include littlenecks. Not to worry gentle readers, I didn't take that as a sign. 

Jason, who served us, and Mike, another server, were relaxed, elegant, and really into making sure that we were well taken care of, in a low-key way. I noticed that the table next to ours was eating some sort of fried thing and I asked Mike about it. It was the Fried Shrimp, Lemon and Herb Mayonnaise plate. I enquired if we might just have some fried lemon--because FRIED LEMON you guys?!?! And magically, a few minutes later, Mike whispered up to our table with a small dish of said lemon and mayonnaise. We agreed that we could eat a much larger portion of these things, easily. Perhaps too easily. And suggested that were it to be offered as a plate, we'd have to become regulars. Mike demurred and mentioned that he might let the Chef know. 

The point here is this: excellent service isn't just about having a seamless experience, it's about working with people who know their stuff and want you to have the very best experience you can, under their careful, gracious execution. It's also about creating a sense of ease and wonder, thereby hooking you into dining with them again. It worked y'all. 

These folks should be running the country. 

Thanks, Wildair. We had a lovely time!
Very so so. Food was mediocre and staff was the same.  Pretty overpriced for what is going on. You know what I mean?
Is this a bar or a restaurant? This restaurant was way over-hyped! We were so disappointed with our time spent here.

Great experience! 

Group had turnips, lettuce salad, beef tartar, skate, scallops crudo and pork Milanese and both desserts of the day. 

Super fresh ingredients and the flavors were all amazing. Plates are small minus the pork Milanese but still very shareable. 

The desserts were great too... Not to sweet and the popcorn granita (?) was refreshingly unique.
Interesting wines, good food (the sweet potato dish is a must), and a knowledgable staff. Definitely worth checking out.

Came here as a group of 4. The space is very intimate and small so be prepared to wait during peak weekend hours. A little disappointed that they only had 3 cocktails but my americano spritz was delightful. We ordered oysters, clams (maybe the best prepared clams I've come across), bread, fried shrimp (they also fry lemons so be careful what you eat), skate, persimmon and straciatella cheese, and beef tartare. All plates were petite but enough for all four of us to try a couple bites of each. They were all very good! Both desserts - chocolate hazelnut tart, and panda cotta were delicious!

Been wanting to try this place but was deterred by the supposedly long wait. Finally went on a Tuesday night and NO WAIT! Food was tapa style small plates and they have a few bottles of interesting wines on their list from less popular regions which I always appreciate. 
Space is tight, and the three of us end up ordering almost every vegetable and seafood dishes on the menu. Their grain salads are better than what the description promised, so don't leave out the greens. All the food we tasted were great, the 2 bottles of Slovenian sparkling rose were delish, and the last bottle of orange wine we tried was just different enough to end our night on an interesting note..Overall a great experience! will come back with girlfriends next time.

Fun atmosphere. The food was pretty good, but the place is a bit over-hyped IMO. After the second bottle of wine showed up to our table already opened, I had to ask why they did not open the bottles at the table. Strange etiquette for a restaurant with a wine list.

I went there during their first month of opening and I feel that the restaurant was over-hyped. After reading articles online saying that it may be the best new restaurant in NYC, I had high expectation and decided to give it a try. The two of us went there on a weekday dinner and there was only like a 5 minute wait. 
The restaurant was really small (not unlike other Manhattan restaurant) and had a industrial & simplistic kind of atmosphere. 

We order a bunch of appetizers like steak tartar, fried squid, Georgia white shrimp, and Uni on potato. Even though the presentations are nice, the food are all over-salted and the flavor was not well developed probably due to the long line of people waiting outside and the chef were just trying to get the food out as soon as they can.
The wine selection wasn't great, but the wine we had was very nicely chosen by the server to pair with our food.

I would say that the food here is slightly above average in Manhattan but definitely not a restaurant I would recommend to wow another foodie friend.

Tips:
+ the atmosphere was more like a bar than a restaurant for romantic date
+ with the amount of salt they put on their food, beer will probably be better than wine for pairing

I loved every dish we tried, and we tried a LOT for just two of us. We had finished and our neighbors at the next table said we had to get the tartare for dessert..... so what the hell we did. And a dessert. And they brought out another dessert to celebrate my friend's birthday. And guys, the XO clams are as good as I hoped they'd be. People have talked this place up but I was very very pleased. I'd love for this to be a go-to neighborhood spot for me but I live a little too far for that.

I seriously crave their beef tartare and I don't even eat red meat that often...

Other really delicious dishes: potato darphin/uni...just order your own, hard to share this! Sourdough bread/olive oil, and pork milanese...other dishes are great as well but every time I'm here, these are a must. 

Just wish they'd take reservations...unless you're here when they open, you'll have to wait.

Possibly the worst wine selection I've ever seen.
I had to send back the first bottle after tasting it and the second was no better.

Very small dishes and overpriced.

$100 wagyu for two should've been a $65 wagyu for one.

The food is decent, the prices and sizes are ridiculous. Would not go back.

I have been meaning to try this place for a while now after all of the great things I've read. Walked in around 7:45 and only had to wait 30 minutes, was expecting a longer wait. Got 2 seats right at the chef's counter and the service from the start was great. Wildair is very casual but elegant, perfect for neighborhood and any day of the week dinner. Overall I thought the restaurant was OK, will not be back. Below are my ratings of the dishes we ordered. 

Bread 4/5
*Mentioned to us by the server that it was a signature dish, we figured why not
Scallop Crudo 3/5
*Was expecting more from this. Did not impress me 
Beef Tartar 4/5
*This was great, a must order. A little too saucy but still fantastic. 
Fried Shrimp 3/5
*Lightly battered and flavorful but I could definitely have lived without it
Wagyu Steak 2/5
*So disappointing. The waitress told us that the cut was from Colorado, however from our knowledge Wagyu is Japanese. Steak was not tender, juicy and hard to cut. For the price of $100, I expected something memorable. Do not order.

Tried to eat here tonight (around 8pm on a Thursday night). Place didn't seem super busy as there were a couple open tables. I waited just inside the front door for nearly 5 minutes and watched 3 staff members walk within 2 feet of me (including one person walk by 3 times) without anyone saying a word to me or even making eye contact. Pathetic! Seems the good reviews have gone to their heads.

The food is good, some of it very good, though  nothing extraordinary.  Why, I wonder, do people put up with  the "experience" (to quote our waitress) of deafening music and uncomfortable chairs.  There's plenty of good food in NY that doesn't come with a musical assault so why, I wonder, is this place so popular.  What am I missing?  Please, someone, explain the "fun" that requires screaming at your dinner companion rather than having normal, civilized conversation.

Easily in my top 5 restaurants in NYC.  The second opening from the Contra Team (next door) and more of a low key menu as opposed to a tasting menu.  But low key does not lower the standards.  I love every dish they have and I think I've tried every one.  Highlights include the bread, calamari (nine better), spicy tuna, clams...ok the highlights are the whole menu.  Beer selection is very limited but quality, however you are coming here for the wine.  The wait can be a difficult thing if you're not there are 6 but good places to drink a beer nearby while waiting.

I came to this place with high expectations after reading reviews of it being the best new restaurant in New York etc and while the food is not bad I was pretty disappointed.

Food:
We ordered the steak tartare, which was good but nothing special and there are many better in New York. I feel like the taste isn't so original and isn't as good as your traditional French steak tartare. It was very expensive for what I would say is an average dish.

We also had this fish (it has been a while since I had there so I am forgetting but I believe it was mackerel or perhaps sardine) with a type of yuzu butter. The yuzu butter was quite unique and I commend them for a bit of unique innovation but it wasn't super great. Also the fish tasted like it came from a can not fresh at all. Honestly with these prices you shouldn't serve canned fish, an absolute disgrace.

We also had the bread which was good but not good enough to pay 5 dollars for.


The service was pretty poor for a place with these prices. When I asked for salt for the olive oil (that came with the bread) the waiter quickly and rudely dismissed me and said "it already has salt". His manner and tone was incredibly rude and I do not pay such high prices to be spoken to like that. Other than that the service was inattentive and despite not many people being there (it was quite early), I did not feel comfortable.

In the end this place is nowhere near as innovative as it thinks, it has incredibly overpriced underwhelming food (honestly canned fish really??) and I would suggest not going.

Food was good but with the myriad of good food in the city I would be hard pressed to say one should rush to the restaurant to try it. 

Also if you think this is a wine bar think again. Wines by the glass are super limited and all the wines are "all natural".  I read one post here that was comparing these "French originating" wines to California wines as the yelper correctly identified that these are much earthier. However, as someone who has traveled France extensively just to drink their wine - trust me this is not what the French drink. And after one sip you'll realize why.

Had an awesome dinner. We got the crudo, beef tartar, persimmon and skate dishes. Crudo was the only thing that wasn't memorable. But damn was the tartar, persimmon and fish amazing. Bread should be free but whatevs. Everything was supremely delicious! Oh my goodness and the DESSERT? I don't even care for desserts but the Hazelnut tart and Panna Cotta was out of this world orgasm good. YUM!

After waiting an hour and a half for a table on a Thursday night, we were still really excited about sitting down to a long-anticipated meal. Unfortunately, we were not very impressed once we finally got our food. Maybe we had unrealistic expectations because of all the hype? We left unsatisfied at the end of our meal which shouldn't happen and has left me in a state of confusion. 

I wouldn't discourage anyone from going here but I also wont be rushing back any time soon.

I would rate this 1 out of 10 based on food and environment.  But because of the Okay service i am giving it 2 stars.

Wildair has been on my radar for the last month or 2.  Ever since it was nominated for the James Beard award for best new restaurant.  It seems to be a casual small winebar serving small plates.

Getting a table:

Wildair unlike sister restaurant Contra which is 2 doors down is a first come first serve establishment.  Which means on the weekends get there before 7 to be able to catch a bite before a reasonable time.  We put our name down around 630 and was told a 1 hour wait.  After coming back at 7 we saw a lot of empty tables but was not able to be seated til 740.  Nite cap down the road is a nice place to grab a drink.

Ambiance:

Once seated in one of the cramped bar seats, one quickly realizes how small and loud the space is.  The loudness and the cramped environment i looked past thinking the food would be good. But the place is dark, minimal lighting.  It took a while for the waitress to come with the wine menu and water.  Noticed that my water glass was dirty could not track down someone for a new one.  Cleanliness is a pet peeve of mine.  There is a pretentiousness to it as if they know what food and wine is better than you do.  

The wine list:

If you do decide to drink as this is a winebar,  You would expect a vast list of wines by the glass.  The wine list online shows a large amount of different varieties that one has never really heard of from France.  They said all their wines are natural.  I don't know what they mean by natural.  On the list i would say in total there is less than 10 wine by the glass combining sparking, white and reds.  Not many options.  Their online list does not tell you this.  The way the list uses words that you have never heard of or seen just eeks pretentiousness.  

So we ordered some glasses of whites they were okay nothing to write home about.

Food:

I was excited by the menu online even though limited in selection.  The menu on the day we went had alot less items of interest.

We had 4 things.

The bread and olive oil.  I understand charging for the bread if it was amazing.  But buying a forccacio at eataly and eating it with your favorite olive oil and maldon salt would be far superior.

The scallop crudo.
This is no crudo.  The scallops where diced and hidden under a blanket of thin sliced radishes.  The dish had a super vinegary and an after thought of spice taste to it.  This was almost inedible.  The scallops should be the main focus of a crudo but it was not and execution and taste was poor.  On another note the pine nuts aka the 4th ingredient contributed nothing to this dish.

The beef tartare

A tartare that has cheese and chopped nuts on top.   The beef quality was mediocre almost tough.  The dish did not come together well.  By this point i have pretty much given up on this place.

The last dish is the pork milanese

This is basically a large pork chop.  with some greens and sauce on the side.  The pork chop was not juicy or seasoned well.  It was bland.

Even though i would have like to try more dishes and their deserts based on the poor dishes we decided to leave.

Maybe we went on an off night as the front of house was also helping with waitress.  Maybe they are short staffed.  But i am not looking to come back anytime soon.

Definitely one of my top 5 restaurants in New York. Finally managed to go back again and this time everything was perfect. Food was excellent, as always. Wine, amazing. The service, the best. Thank you wildair for a lovely meal. Hope to visit again soon, if i can manage the 2 hour wait.

no idea what the hype is about.  Food was fine but nothing extraordinary.  Room was crowded, just a touch too loud to have a conversation, and food came out randomly even when 2 entrees were ordered that should have been served together.  

Oh and if anyone in your party doesn't want alcohol they'll have to be ok with water - no tea or soda available.

AMAZING! The ingredients were all so fresh; we shared the potato darphin with uni, the fluke crudo, the corn salad, and an order of warm bread, topped of with some tasty gin and tonics. It was packed but the service was still fast and the space had a wonderful ambiance. The jalapeños really added heat to the darphin with uni. We got the 'nduja on the side with the fluke which was a better choice I think, and the corn salad, also simple in thought was executed brilliantly. The restaurant is casual but the food feels upscale- great for a meeting with friends or more formal sit-down.

Named one of America's best new restaurants of the year by Bon Appetite, Wildair feels more like a casual, intimate neighborhood spot on the Lower East Side than a fine dining destination.  Its unassuming nature belies a sophisticated menu of tasty small shareable plates.  A little on the bright side (which is great for taking food pictures), the restaurant is very small. If you turn your head to the back, you can see the open kitchen and the staff busy at work. 

Wildair does not take reservations so get there early. Luckily, my group of six was able to get a table by 8:30 with only an hour and a half wait on a Friday night.

French wine is the big draw here, especially the "Pet'Nat" wines which have been naturally fermented.  From the Bon Appetite article, I knew to get wines that were stored in the magnum-sized bottles since the Chef prefers these wines.  If you're not used to french wines, it is nothing like your typical California wines. French wines tend to be a lot more earthier, musty and woodsy in my opinion - tasting more of its "terroir."

All of the small plates are meant to be shared which is great when you want to try everything like me. 

Favorite dishes:  
Roman Lettuce wedges and pistachio - light and refreshing
Beef tartare, smoked cheddar, chestnut - beef tasted clean, almost like tuna 
corn with schmaltz (or rendered chicken fat) - gave the corn a nice richness 
green salad with crispy grains - expected crunch from the crispy rice, I actually mixed it with the beef tartare to give it more texture

Okay Dishes:
Pork milanese, gribiche, mustard greens - I've had better. 
Fried squid, spring onion, lemon, basil - only gripe is that everything is fried, so you might unexpectedly bite into a lemon instead of squid
Tuna toast - toast was a little too over-toasted
Shisito peppers - had better, actually best ones I've had was in Atlanta at Staplehouse

The desserts of hazelnut tart and panna cotta with granita were just okay, almost like an afterthought

Amazing! Had oysters, spicy tuna toast, beef tartare, crudo and finished it off with the chocolate hazelnut tart. Everything was delicious, unique and well thought out. I am blown away by these chefs and can't wait to try out Contra.

We really enjoyed our meal here.  Love the atmosphere and service and the food was creative and excellent.

We had the bread, the crudo, the gem lettuce, the spicy tuna, the fried squid, and the pork milanese.  We gave 4 of the 5 dishes 5 stars.  They were all delicious, except for the squid.  The squid was way too salty and the squid ink aoli did not add any flavor.  By contrast, the pork was perfectly fried and salted - tender in the middle and super crunchy outside.  We had the panna cotta for dessert, which I really dug but my wife thought was just OK.  

Bottom line, we loved it!
Amazing! Fluke, corn, beef tartare, radishes, and desserts were all outrageously amazing. Worth the wait!

Exciting times call for exciting food. Yet another friend's bittersweet goodbye and dinner at Wildair qualify.

Before I forget, the service was top-notch to say the least, from the first moment I walked to the front, my friend arrived a bit later, the host noticed and spoke to me. Phenomenal as she wasn't even standing there but making her rounds and spotted me as I was trying not to be noticed. And the service continued to be great, in checking on us, and in the food coming to us without a super long wait like it does in many superb dining restaurants. 

Did someone say superb? Made me think of the fried squid with black ink aioli, aka the "winner" as my friend happily called it. Its shiny, black, and very unusual dipping sauce attracted the attention of the tables sitting next to us. We kept hearing "What's that?!" over and over and over again... 

If that wasn't enough to make us feel like the rockstars we secretly are--I'm normally too cool or rather, too old for dinner on the LES, or I like to pretend that I am which is why I hadn't been there in so long before this dinner--the taste certainly was. I couldn't get enough of the aioli and they gave us an ample amount. But I kinda wanted to inhale it. The squid itself was cooked perfectly, not chewy at all but meaty and just a divine texture. We took our time to savor it.Talked about Texas, her future career moves and her now fiancé. 

Before the superstar squid, we had the little gem lettuces that we both agreed looked especially delicious but there was some taste component missing, sweetness or savoriness perhaps. It was just a bit too tangy and needed some onions or cheese to round it out. You'd think the pistachios would give it that sweet-ish flavor but alas it didn't. The conversation was at its thickest moment of gossip about work.

Before the lettuces, we had the sensational Potato darphin, aka close runner up to the squid. There's just something about uni --sea urchin-- that no one can deny is crave-worthy. And in this dish, paired with a crispy potato croquette, you probably want to get your own. We managed to share one, but I believe it's unsharable and worth it to enjoy knowing that you have all that luscious, complex uni flavor, with the expected nature and texture of a deep fried home fry, to yourself. We had just waited an hour for dinner and were talking about the first place we visited while waiting. The food there was simple, comfort food and the ambiance matched it. 

It wasn't at all like the special plates and very NYC modern day tapas vibe that Wildair has claimed its own.

The welcoming staff makes this place a success. Non-wine experts, don't be intimidated by the menu. Our waiter immediately made us feel comfortable in sharing very basic things we like/dislike about wine ie) enjoy honey notes, dislike high acidity, dislike oaky, prefer dry over fruity, etc. He thoroughly described a few bottles for us, and we were able to reach an agreement on what turned out to be one of the best whites I've ever tasted. It really makes a difference when your wait staff takes the time to listen, answer your questions and lead you to a high quality bottle. Keep it up Wildair!

The thing about Wildair is that they're doing things other people are doing, they're just doing it in a way that will ruin it for you everywhere else: oysters, shishitos, warm bread & grassy olive oil. All better here. And the fluke crudo, forget about it. What a gorgeous little feat. 

Don't bother looking at the wine list and pretending (even if you're a wine geek), just tell them what you want to eat and ask for something amazing to go with.

4 words: WAGYU STEAK FOR 2. Yes please, still dream of this dish.

This restaurant really impressed me with the food! The restaurant is tiny (you'll hear other conversations, touch elbows, see a missed eyebrow hair on another dinner guest, etc...) and the waits are long. On a Saturday night we weren't seated until 10 (walked around LES to kill time for an hour) - doesn't bother us, but for some people this may be too late. There is no bar inside to grab a drink at and wait. But worth the wait, and it quiets down by 10 because most people are leaving when you are starting.

We shared a romaine salad, it was chilled, crisp and had a pleasant variety of flavors in the light dressing from fresh herbs and pistachio. It was refreshing and needed because then we ordered straight up raw, or near raw, beef. We got the beef tartare and both appreciated the subtle differences from many of the traditional/classic tartares that dot so many menus, differences such as smoky cheddar and chestnuts on top - I liked the crunch. And was no raw egg for another difference. Very mild beef flavor, cold and light. I would highly recommend it! 

Then the aforementioned wagyu, dry-aged as well - just delectable. Warm, juicy, fatty, salty (maybe they could have eased up here) and mild - every thinly sliced bite was so satisfying. The vinegary-carrots were a great flavor combination to the beef, and the mild white sauce (I'll be honest, I don't remember what it was, but it was creamy and light. It was not needed, but did complement the beef). If you are a carnivore and can handle your meat slightly warm because it's nearly raw, you'll like this, otherwise it might scare you. And honestly three people could easily share this and feel satisfied. Our waiter recommended the Francois Ecot Avec ou Sans Mercure wine to go with our meal and it was perfect - it was low in tannins and lighter bodied. 

Lastly, when you go, if the panna cotta is on the dessert menu get it. When we went in the spring, the fruit was strawberry. It was the icing on the cake for us - perfectly smooth panna cotta, tangy strawberry, and sweet crunchy milk crumbles that had a touch of salt.

amending since Yelp's auto-screener is blocking this review...
several weeks ago our party of 2 tried to eat at Wildair. horrible front of the house--despite 4-top tables being occupied by 2 people, and one 4-top open, the hostess would only offer us seats facing brick wall. when asked about the open 4-top she said it was "reserved"--but Wildair's website implies NO rez--it says "Walk Ins Only".

we have no intention of going there again, despite the Bon Appetit rave...going out to eat means good Service, Food AND Ambience--NOT at Wildair--too many options in NYC to spend our food $$$....

Great spot.  Suggested white wine, a Chablis, was excellent and went well with all of our dishes, even the beef tartare. Oysters were fresh and a great beginning.  We needed one more dish after all the others and added the tuna--wow, so glad we had this to finish our meal, though all dishes and suggested dishes were very good.

Wildair is a LES gem - wow, the food speaks for itself. Our server was extremely tentative and very knowledgable. Young female with some sort of accent, very pleasant. (AURORE) I would have gave Wildair 4 stars if the hostess did a better job. We arrived (party of 3) on a random Thursday night, we were told it was an hour wait, fine, and we gave our contact #. We grabbed a few drinks at Hotel Rivington. We started walking back since it was about an hour and 15 minutes and no call. We arrived and there were 4 tables inside that could have easily sat us, the hostess (curly brown hair with glasses) came over, saw that I was upset, and says she was about to call us. Thats complete BS as all 4 tables were bussed, cleaned and reset probably 20 minutes ago. I wonder if we didn't show up if she would have called us at all. I don't know, she probably thought we were broke, even though I'm pretty sure we had one of the biggest checks of the night.

The wagyu steak was cooked perfect, probably don't need the peas, maybe a different green.

Pork milanese was fantastic.

Crudo was fantastic.

Shrimp was just ok, having to break it down was a bit annoying.

All the salads were great.

The best thing about this place is the wine list. There are so many reasonable bottles and a wide, interesting selection of unusual wines. The food is generally good too but certain dishes are hit or miss and I still object to paying for bread that is no better than that served at most restaurants in NYC. Service is highly inconsistent: sometimes friendly and cheerful and other times pretty rude. It's loud too. Really loud on weekends.

First off, I've never been to Contra, although I do plan to go there eventually. Second, I went to Wildair on a whim. I was standing outside, looking at the menu and my boyfriend said "it doesn't look like they have food." I said quite the contrary. It wasn't until he had eaten half a loaf of delicious bread and olive oil that we were on the same page. The bread was a hit, as were the shishitos, but I don't think they take much. I had a glass of white wine which was delicious, but definitely leaned sweet. The shrimp were amazing, and a bonus that they were from the States and not Asia, but I will say they were messy. Shrimp with the shell on is hard to eat daintily. The potato with uni was insane. I do love potato pancakes, but I felt the uni was the real standout here. 
All in all, a good experience and I think we will go back as the menu changes over time. A good place to try new things.

Still incredible. Here's our ranking from our latest visit:

- Fluke crudo, pineapple, 'nduja
- Chocolate hazelnut tart
- Beef tartare, smoked cheddar, brazil nuts
- Selection of cheeses
- Bread and olive oil
- Littleneck clams, XO, bitter almond
- Blistered shoshito peppers, nama yuba
- Crispy grain salad, hearts of palm, tarragon

I really can't stress enough how great the fluke was, with the pineapple and sausage. Very different from any other dish I can remember eating, and just perfect in its own way.

There was also a gap between the peppers and the salad -- I liked the salad, but my wife wasn't crazy about it, and I thought it was easily my least favorite. It was the only dish out of eight that I didn't totally love.

Also: for our second consecutive visit, they didn't have the spicy tuna, scallion, and tomatoes, which looks amazing. I'm dying to try this, so hopefully we get this next time.

Fun, playful, and tasty dishes in a warm and casual space.

Service was friendly and everything was brought out at a really good pace. However, I did take issue with our waitress, who was also friendly, but whose wine recommendation ended up being nothing like the description she gave or the notes I had said I was looking for. 
Aside from this minor thorn in my side, the food and ambience are really awesome and Wildair is certainly worth checking out. Here are the dishes we had, ranked from my most to least favorite:  

Fluke Crudo
This dish I feel like embodies the creative and fun spirit of Wildair, and the interesting choices taken definitely paid off. The fluke is cut like a ceviche, and in a very lemony dressing, with the nduja sausage used more as a flavoring, in a non-overwhelming, but certainly present way. Ultimately, I kept going back for more (it was a great portion, I should also add) and if you have the chance I would get this dish. 

Beef Tartare
The beef is treated more like a ceviche dish than a beef tartare, and it comes in an aggressively vinegary dressing. The combination of the beef, cheese, and vinegar make for an addictive dish that's far from a fatty, hearty tartare but that fits the seafood-based menu of Wildair perfectly. 

White Georgian Shrimp
These shrimp are fat, shell-on, and grilled to tasty perfection. The shrimp themselves were awesome and perfectly cooked, with the perfect amount of charcoal flavor, though I thought the sauce could have been better; it was oily and had a take-out Chinese food taste to it. Still worth ordering though, by my measure. 

Seaweed Butter Radishes
These were really tasty and great to snack on (say if you were just coming in for some wine). 

Littleneck Clams
The dressing--XO sauce and almond milk--was amazing, and hit all right right notes, and the dish was really tasty and addictive. However, I thought the clams were a little too briny, if I had to make a comment. 

Fried Squid
The squid was tender, fatty, and almost porky. A+ on however they treated it to get it that way. However, the batter was really sweet, and I wish this came with some acid (a lemon?) to cut the richness with. The sauce was also meh, but again, like with all of this dishes, this one is still awesome and worth ordering. 

We finished off with the already-famous hazelnut tart, which was scrumptious to the last bite--the aggressive saltiness and decadent real hazelnut cream were amazing, and I feel like the dessert reflects the rest of the menu; dishes that take calculated risks that totally pay off. We really enjoyed every dish we had, and the playfulness made it such a great dining experience. For the reasonable price, the fun ambience, and the playful dishes, I would say this place gets my stamp of approval. Wildair, I'll be back for you!

Very unique menu. The seats are uncomfortable and tables are quite small. But it's a small space so I understand but just be aware. The service was very good. All the dishes were things I had never had before, but few were things I would order again. My favorite was the gem lettuce crusted with pistachios. The clams were not up my alley, very strongly flavored. The dishes were all very salty, even the panna cotta dessert! The bread was delicious.

Nice restaurant, interesting combinations, I particularly like the salted cod and the Hokkaido Uni. Usually weird fusion disinterests me but this place has some good fusion, some might complain that it's a bit salty overall:) I think it was ok the way it is.

Be warned, Wildair has a sick salt fetish. And I do not mean that as a compliment. Much of its food is verging on inedible due to insane amounts of salt. So much so that one member of my party was actually sickened after eating the chocolate salted caramel tart dessert. Let's take it from the top. 

When the best dish on the menu is warm bread with quality olive oil, there is a problem. That is all I really wanted to eat here, and I can go to an Italian bakery to get that. 

The clams (literally served on piles of salt), had well enough flavor served in an XO cognac broth inside the half shell. I myself am not a fan of soupy clams but my friend ordered a second dish of this. I also found the sprigs on top were distracting to eating. Would have been better chopped. 

The soft shell crab was a terrible disappointment! It was fried too heavy with greasy batter and came on a bed of thick fatty orange colored plain sauce, (possibly the salt was remarkably missed here). Needed LOTS of acid to counteract the heaviness. Not just half a lime that was served. 

One of my party tasted the salted cod and just about spit it out. She said it tasted disgusting! It was hemorrhaging salt!

The Georgia white shrimp's savory flavor was acceptable but not strong enough. The shrimp itself was also hard to eat. Did not peel easily and you had to devein as you ate. Another member of my group was extremely annoyed at the mess and hassle that ensued. Payoff was too low for the effort to clean the shrimp at the table.

Two of us ordered the wagyu beef. They should be ashamed to serve us almost raw steak when we ordered medium rare. The vegetables served had an off putting smoky flavor that didn't endear. The steak was doused with unnecessary heavy chunks of salt that attacked our tastebuds as we ate. Cringe...

As aforementioned, the overly salted chocolate dessert was sickening. The only other dessert offered, the panna cotta had distracting red berry flavored crunchy ice, over a silky pudding layer with crumble. I don't know about you, but I don't go to a restaurant to be fed ice chips to freeze my teeth. It was a relief to be free of the salt at that point though. 

We told the waiter we found the food to be too salty but he just shrugged and said yeah, it is. 

After seeing the subpar soft shell crab, we had canceled the second order for it. We were charged for it and had to have the bill reprinted. So poor attention to detail on the servers' part.

At times we were without much needed water too. No worse punishment for over salted food!

I have heard of this place from several hardcore foodie friends that inform me the critics are raving. I left this place aghast at whomever these critics are. Like the chef here, they must clearly also have a very unhealthy obsession with salt. Perhaps they are smokers with dead palates?!

My verdict: Save your money ($100+ for one person, no drinks) and go elsewhere.

What a meal it is. And certainly one of the more memorable ones I have eaten this year. From start to finish, every dish is strong, thoughtful and well-executed. For me, I would even take this over the flagship restaurant because of the casualness of the dining atmosphere. Moreover, having it a la carte means you can share and also not be pressured to eat through a multi-course dinner. The ingredients are fresh here and the cooking style/techniques are quite inventive. This is definitely one of the spots I will be on the look out for in the year to come. Next step, checking if they would allow outside bottles. This place would be a great wine dinner candidate...

Full dish-by-dish review can be found here:

http://www.higrubandgrog.com/stories/2015/11/30/wildair-the-cousin-of-contra

This place was excellent.  Very upscale dining experience in a casual, relaxed ambiance in the LES.  Went on a Tuesday night around 8:30pm and had no problem getting a seat.  Nice day and had the window open so we had a fresh breeze.  Ordered the beef tartare which was really great, topped with crunchy hazelnuts and cheese, pork rilette, bread & assorted cheeses to start.  We went a little overboard with the appetizers but they were all very tasty.  We started off with some sparkling white wine which was great. All of their wines are natural and the waitress was able to ask us what we liked and offer her recommendations which was very helpful. For entrees we split the pork milanese  (maybe not the right choice as this place seems to be known for their unique plates, but it was excellent nonetheless.  Finished off with two glasses of rose wine and their chocolate tart and panna cotta.  Both amazing and inventive.  Definitely don't leave without getting the tart. Taking a star off b/c prices are a little steep but your dishes are made with care.  You won't be disappointed.

It took me way too long to make it into Wildair. 

After almost a year and far too many accolades, I finally had the opportunity to check out one of the most buzzed abound restaurants in lower Manhattan. From an overwhelming majority of Yelp reviews to local food blogs to critics from esteemed publications, it seems Wildair is a universal hit. I can't say I disagree. 

Moseyed in on a Friday night at 6:00pm sharp. With only a handful of other restaurant goers waiting in line ahead of me (it's walk up only), we had our pick of the litter for seating. Being a fan of chef's tables and eating at counters, we chose the high tops with a direct view into the efficient, minuscule kitchen Wildair cooks and chefs operate from. It's impressive to watch this team pump out high quality food in such tight confines in about the same time it takes you humble brag to your friends on Snapchat. With such a small restaurant, I'm sure their strategy is to turn over seats in as quick, yet non-invasive a fashion as possible. If you're in a hurry, but still want to eat something other than a dirty water Sabrett, you can make that happen with ease.

My lovely lady and I shared the beef tartare, bread with olive oil, purple sweet potato salad, and a chocolate tart. The beef tartare came decorated with smoked cheddar and chestnut, and was an excellent choice for fans of raw beef. The purple sweet potato salad was a sleeper hit, easily our favorite dish of the bunch. I'm sure the menu rotates based on food availability, but you should target this dish if it's featured the day you visit. Despite foul cries that bread and oil should come complimentary at a restaurant, I have no problem paying for something as enjoyable as hot and delicious fresh baked bread. To those who find the notion unscrupulous, just a quick reminder that it's not the '80s anymore. You probably stopped wearing Z Cavariccis, and well made bread may cost you a few bucks. Restaurant margins are razor thin these days, y'all. 

Rounding out the meal, our chocolate tart was simple, yet perfect for closing the loop on dinner. Not too sweet, topped with thick sea salt, and sitting atop a homemade dough constructed of crumbled pralines and plenty of butter. I'd return just for this and an espresso if it were possible. 

If you've been wondering if it's worth they hype, I'd venture to say it is. It can be spendy for small plates, but there's more to life than never ending pasta bowls. Savor something brilliant, enjoy the moment, and you'll be just fine.

Okay, I have been wanting to come here since I learned supposedly this place is better than Contra.
I've been to Contra and since they take reservations, it was easier to go there than here. Since all of my friends are pretty much impatience people.

Finally came here with A, two weeks ago and it was a rainy Friday, so lucky for us, there were plenty of seats available.

I had a birthday get together to go to and plus this place didn't have any cocktails that I wanted to drink, so we both didn't drink any cocktails here.

We shared the following:

Bread - same thing at Contra. It was good.

Pork Rilette - decent, but still dying for the Salmon Rilette at Nomad.

Potato darphin, uni, jalapeno - eh, nothing special.

A asked the waitress if we should do the shrimp or the soft shell crab, the waitress recommended we go with the soft shell crab. When we got it and I biting into the meat, I was like gross, I asked A if the soft shell crab tasted and smelled fishy. A said, yeah, that's because you know it's fresh. I am like no, that's a sign that you know it's not fresh and knowing the fact that most deliveries comes on a Tuesday, I am sure the waitress was trying to sell us old crabs. I have never had any issues with soft shell crab until I came here.

I got sick off that soft shell crab - this place, I don't get it, why is there a line and why do people rave about the food here.

They can't even serve fresh soft shell crab.

Got this recommendation from a bartender in the nomad. Did not disappoint. Hour wait on a Saturday at 6:45. They do not take reservations but will text you when table is ready and ask "you still down?" Plenty of bars in the area to pass the time. Small place, unbelievably uniquely fresh fresh food. The grain salad- OUTRAGEOUS. Staff super friendly and helpful with the unfamiliar menu. Will be back.

our bread and olive oil
yo... this bread is good.

potato darphin, uni, jalapeno
it's hash browns with sea urchin. it's wild good.

beef tartare, smoked cheddar, chestnut
the smoked cheddar set it off.

fried squid, spring onion, lemon, basil
the squid ink aioli would be good on anything. fried slices of lemon are not for me, but everything else was on point.

pork milanese, gribiche, mustard greens
a piece of fried pork? do it.

panna cotta, (insert fruit) granita, (insert flavor) crumble
this is my favorite dessert anywhere. i've had several different versions and it's been good every time.

wine
personally, i don't know anything about wine, but the staff at wildair will lead you down the right path.

mahon (gin y tonica)
it's okay. stick to wine.

vago mezcal espadin (negroni)
see above.

*****

wildair is one of the best restaurants in the city.

Was here at 6 and it was already filling up. Our party of 3 did not get seated at a table til everyone arrived. In the meantime I ordered a glass of red campania while waiting for my friends to show up. It was super tart and not deserving of the price. They told me they just opened the bottle but after 15 minutes it was still pretty tart so I let them know and they took back the glass. We ordered a bottle of red instead and when they opened it for us to try it was also super tart. We finally settled on another bottle which tasted decent. Onto the food. We ordered the pork rillette, bread with olive oil, cheese plate and meats. Pork rillette was a small serving. Didn't knock my socks off. The cheese and meats were ok. We ordered the bass crudo which had a good balance of acidity and flavor. The fried squid was too hard. The breading was too heavy. I think they should go lighter on the breading. The squid ink sauce was too salty. Onto dessert. The Panna cotta with milk crumb. It was like a deconstructed Panna cotta which I did like. The sweet and saltiness of the crumb and the berry granita made the Panna cotta stand out. The texture and flavors mixed together was a hit for me.

Very disappointing considering the standards that were set by Contra :( the only positives were the Georgia white shrimp, our bread and evoo and the fluke ceviche. Everything else just felt flat and made you say huh? The biggest disappointment was the fried squid!!!! It was overly battered to mask the main ingredient and over seasoned to an extent that tasted like Cheetos? Yes Cheetos.

We were refused service so I cannot comment on the food. The manager/ waitress (short, about 5'5" blonde woman) would not sit is because they were holding the table for somebody else. The website says they don't take reservations, but they're were holding TWO different tables for parties who were not yet at the restaurant. The hostess said that the party of 6 would be back "right away", but even after 10 minutes they didn't show up. When we brought this up to her and asked if we could be seated she flat out refuses us service and walked off. In outraged because the restaurants website specifically says they do not take reservations. I gladly would have made a reservation, but instead I was denied service for no good reason. We ended up leaving, and the waitress was laughing at us as we walked off. 

tl:dr: rude manager/waitress (short blonde woman), gave a party preference who was not yet at the restaurant, after telling us "it's first come first serve", then flat or refused is service. Maybe she was racist because we were a group of black and Asian people. 

This restaurant has a false reservation policy, rude and racist staff members who will turn you away and laugh at you. This all happened at 6:30pm on Friday April 15, 2016. This waitress/manager has no place working with people and deserves to be fired. I'll be going back to the restaurant to speak with the manager later.

P.S. We went there to celebrate my birthday.
At this point the only birthday present I'd like is to see this woman lose her job and never work in another respectable restaurant again. I hear the food is great, so it's unfortunate this low life worker is tarnishing the reputation of a place with the same head chef as Contra.

Its 2016 and you figured that not being able to be seated because of your race wouldnt exist anymore especially if you live in NY. Well be assured it does in does in this establishment. Came with a group of non-white friends and was denied service. They dont do reservations, walked in, saw 2 tables for 5 and 4 people, and a short caucasian lady with blonde hair just said no they wont serve us. We tried to ask why, they made an excuse that people has that table taken. At the same time, they do first come first serve, so was confused why TWO tables are being held.

Tried to talk to a manager but the caucasian lady said she was, but she didnt look like the manager, more like a waitress. No place is worth this if they out right treat random people like this.

A girl claiming to be the manager denied me and my party a table that was clearly open saying it was reserved. When I mentioned they don't take reservations she said they would not sit us at all we should go elsewhere. Racism forced us to eat elsewhere.

Decent food, just no particularly standout aspect or dish for me.

Two friends and I stopped by on a Friday evening at 6:15, and we found one of the last few tables available at that time. We split the bread and olive oil, potato darphin, beef tartare, fried squid, and seared tuna between the three of us, and while it was all pretty unique and moderately tasty, and I just didn't find any of the dishes particularly memorable. The potato darphin had a fairly generous heaping of uni, but I didn't find the pairing too tasty, and the fried squid was a tad too breaded for my liking. I did enjoy the beef tartare with the cheddar, although I found the tuna a bit lacking in flavor, and my most favorite dish was probably the chocolate tart dessert. It was generally alright, but if I had waited for an hour to be seated (i.e. if we had arrived 15 minutes later), I probably would have not found it worth the wait.

Yes give me more!:
1.Oysters- I will always want more of these briny bivalves. 
2. Fried Squid- so darn good that we ordered this twice!
3. Claims in almond milk- Doing the happy food dance as I think of this delectable dish. Who knew Almond milk paired will with oysters?
4. Sweet potato, ricotta, tahini- Ricotta. It's got ricotta.
5. Tuna Cabbage Potato- The dish looked unappealing when it arrived. I didn't like the color of the tuna but everyone at the table agreed this dish was unexpectedly delicious. 


I could take it or leave it:
1. Bread and Olive oil- My 4 dinner mates loved it but I don't like to waste precious stomach space on bread.
2. Romaine Lettuces with pistachio- Very good flavors but compared to the other dishes, not so special
3. Potato jalapeno uni- Potato cake was yummy and I normally love anything with spice, but this just didn't do it for me
4. Georgia White Shrimp- extremely tasty but I didn't realize I had to peel the shrimp. 
5. Crudo- This is tasty but if you are only going to order one fish dish, go with the tuna cabbage

The deserts that night were a chocolate something and an orange flavor something that tasted like a creamsicle. Stick with the chocolate something.

The food runs the gamut from the very good (the panna cotta, the wine) to the good but nothing special (the tartare, the cheese plate - though I enjoyed the cayuga blue) to the not very good (fried squid).  Seriously, not sure why people like the fried squid so much.  To me, the batter was too thick relative to the amount of squid in it.  And it seemed like every other bite was biting into a deep fried lemon chunk.  

The service was also inconsistent.  We got in at around 10 pm on a Friday night and are promptly approached by a first staffer who said it would be a few minutes.  A few minutes later, a second staffer (who later turns out to be our server) sees us waiting and says that there is no more seating for the night.  We mention how the first staffer said we would be seated and she seems confused.  After we are seated, the server indicates that they ran out of several things on the menu, including the bread.  We later see the bread being brought out to a party seated much later.  The server was very polite, but everything was very off.  

Unfortunately, another underwhelming dining experience in NYC.

I'm a fan of natural wine and am making my way through New York's establishments. The wine list here is pretty awesome. But what really impressed me here was the food: wow. I loved the Georgia White Shrimp, the Wagyuu, and the Buckwheat Tart. It is totally inspired and inspiring. Hats off to you, Wild Air. Thank you.

Came here for my bday and found it to be very good.  Portions are good and prices are more then fair.  The standout dish to me was the steak tartar . Best ive had, nice acidity, smoked cheddar was a nice touch as were the hazelnuts.  Squid was solid and the desserts were great chocolate tart and panna cotta were something id eat everyday.  Looking foward to coming back and trying some more dishes.

I recommend showing up early - on a Friday night the restaurant opened at 6 pm so we got there right around then and were promptly seated. By 6:30/7 the whole place was full. We snagged the two bar stools facing into the kitchen, and it was fun to watch all the magic happening.

The service was exceptional. Our waitress was lovely and just-the-right-amount attentive. The food itself was also wonderful. 

I've never had a more enjoyable salad at a restaurant in my entire life. Like, seriously. Get the romaine lettuce! It sounds boring but it was outstanding! Trust me. Doused in pistachios and lemon juice and topped with a delicately piped dressing made out of reduced lettuce...unusual but so delicious. The burrata and persimmon salad was equally delicious. Both are must haves.

Next came the delicate beef tartare topped with smoky cheddar and then the potato darphin - basically the best hash brown I have ever had topped with decadent uni and chopped jalapeños. 

The only dish of the evening that we found disappointing was the squid, and that was because the batter was too heavy - you couldn't really taste the seafood. I would recommend passing on this one but make sure not to miss out on any of the others! 

And get the chocolate tart. Just do it. You deserve it.

Super casual, no reservations, small plates for sharing. Ordered 6 plates + 1 dessert for the 2 of us, and everything was at least super interesting, if not mindblowingly delicious (persimmon, potato, hazelnut tart). I lied earlier. Don't share the aforementioned 3 plates. Get an entire order for yourself.

One word: Amazing. If that's not indicative enough of how I feel about Wildair, I instagrammed a collage of my meal here and haven't been able to stop myself from looking back at it whenever the fancy strikes to relive my experience (which, by the way, is embarrassingly often).

Space: Small, casual, and cozy. All communal tables and counter seating - we opted for corner seats by the window, facing the kitchen, so we could watch everything being prepared. 

Service: Staff was warm and incredibly helpful when we inquired about the wine selection (which is all-natural - points! Points!), and was attentive throughout the meal while still giving us our space. 

Food: 

1) House-made bread and olive oil - deceptively simple sounding. If you weren't already in the know about their bread at their sister restaurant Contra next door, you might just pass by this item on the menu - don't. Their bread is incredible - brought back memories of when I was living in France and was spoiled with fresh bread on the daily from the boulanger down the street. It is warm, pillowy and doughy on the inside, and the crust crunches beautifully in the mouth. 

2) Beef tartare - my favorite dish of the meal. A sprinkling of smoked cheddar on top to give it some flavor juxtaposed with the crunch of the chestnuts - texture was incredible.

3) Persimmon, jalapeño, burrata, butternut - I could have passed on this. It was good, but forgettable.

4) Potato darphin with uni - a-freakin-mazing. Maybe I'm biased because I harbor an intense affinity for anything with potato, but this was truly good. Uni was relatively mild. Creamy and tasting vaguely like the sea. 

5) Panna cotta with tangerine granita and crumble - definitely get this over the tart. I'm not normally a dessert person, but this had an airy, light quality that tied up the meal nicely. The tangerine balances the custardy panna cotta beautifully, and the crumble has a nice buttery flavor without feeling too heavy. 

In other words: Go here. Just make sure to come early-ish, as they don't take reservations.

I loved this resto. My type of place, casual but great emphasis on fresh top of the line ingredients and a super knowledgeable and helpful staff. 

Start from the beginning the bread and olive oil were spectacular and gives you a glimpse of what type of restaurant this is. They care deeply and take fantastic pride in delivering amazing bread with a rich deep clean olive oil.  We shared our courses and loved everything we had.  The pork rillette was special.  The pork milanese - deep in porky goodness but with a great crispy crust.  Ok let's move away from the piggy... although i hate doing that.  The roamin lettuces were terrific, loved the beef tartare and wanted more and more of the fried squid. 

If you want a chummy, hip, cool fun spot with great service and inventive food, check wildair out but be prepared to wait a bit as there are no ressies taken...

Not sure how Yelp photos are picked but the one for wild air makes it look like there is a poop (it's a cupcake in fact) next to their name... WildAir protest this...
amazing in everyway.  Highly recommend it. Service, staff and food were fantastic.  The chocolate peanut butter dessert a must have.  Wines all reasonable and natural.

Trendy as hell in a good way. Came in here on a four restaurant food run so we only had a couple of plates. Bass special was ridiculous while the Beef Tartare was ok. We had Rebelle's Beef Tartare earlier in the night and Wildair couldn't hold up.

That being said, if you need an incredibly trendy spot with solid food, Wildair is what you're looking for. I'm coming back

We had an experience at Wildair that, while not flawless, was overwhelmingly positive and would inspire return visits. We were impressed first with the service-- our waiter was highly knowledgeable about the wine list, and when we selected a particular rosé, he warned us that it was very sweet. We were not about that! He directed us instead to an excellent pét-nat, which was actually less expensive than the wine we had originally selected. We highly appreciated the advice and not getting upsold. 

We started with the bread, which costs $4 and is worth it. It is a miscellaneous European-style boule, but with excellent structure and crust. It comes with a very good, grassy Extra Virgin olive oil that was very much to our liking.

We next had the potato darphin with uni,  which is a hashbrown cake topped with picked jalapenos and, naturally, sea urchin. I was expecting this to be a little bland, but the pickled jalapenos made the whole experience very light, and especially with the creamy uni it ended up being very flavorful. 

The fried squid is a fairly standard, though well executed, tempura. Interspersed among the pieces of squid are onion rings and fried lemons, and the tempura batter is opaque enough that you aren't quite sure until you bite in-- which was fun, and like a little joke. The dish was otherwise a little normal for a restaurant that is mostly defined by a sense of whimsy, but it definitely deserves extra points for the excellent squid ink mayo with which it is served.

The white shrimp was easily the low point of the evening. It was solid on flavor, but was served with head, legs, tail, and shell still on. I am no wuss about taking seafood apart but it was a big shrimp and stopping eating to dissect it felt like work. It also got our hands so messy that we had to wash them. It's a misstep, but we appreciated that they were trying something interesting.

It's a really cute space, and a perfect date spot. I highly recommend coming before it opens to snag a table for sure. I'd be excited to come back and see how the menu evolves.

I had a great experience at Wildair. It was the summer, weather was warm, doors were wide open - fantastic ambiance. We almost fought another couple for the last portion of the spicy tuna... sort of kidding about the fight... but it was so good that we just HAD to get seconds. No luck there. 

Everything was fantastic, but what will really bring us back is the tables. You heard right. The tables are really cool, my husband went apesh$t over the fact that he could store his cellphone in the underneath "desk" compartment. I loved the food, he loved the tables... there's something for everybody here.

Don't come out of your way to eat at Wildair, you'll empty your pockets and leave unsatisfied. I can't believe there's a line to get into this place and I can't believe all the good reviews on here. I get that they're trying to do something unique and organic, but none of it tasted particularly good. The uni and potato was flavorless and greasy. The beet plate was the only thing that was good. The bread was ordinary and should've come free, instead they charge you $4 for bread here. The pork milanese was TERRIBLY undercooked, as in bloody, I couldn't eat more than a few bites. The shrimp came in the shell and again was completely bland. Our $50 bottle of wine wasn't even that good. Cramped and very few seats. Communal tables.

If you want to eat disgusting and tastless food and pay a whole lot of money for it, by all means go to Wildair.

Stopped by on a Saturday night around 7pm. Had to wait about an hour but there's a ton of places in the LES to pass the time. 

Got the beef tartare, gem lettuce salad and the shrimp- all were great though portions are on the smaller side so plan accordingly. 

The place itself is extremely small, but I makes for a great ambiance especially if you get a seat near the kitchen area.

I went with a friend on a Thursday night at 7:30 and they quoted us an hour and 15 minute wait, so after spending over an hour at a bar nearby having a drink we returned to Wildair only to be told there were still four groups ahead of us. We ended up having to wait for about 2 hours for a table. I was unimpressed with the selection of cheeses, one was a very hard blue cheese with almost no taste and another seemed like it came from a plastic bag. The best dish was the steak tartare. We also ordered the shrimp dish and the waiter said he would "recommend we eat the shells". I have NEVER been told to eat shrimp shells before, and I even tried to take his recommendation, but almost gagged trying to swallow. We also tried three different wines after asking for a suggestion of a fruit forward pinot noir type, and I don't think the waitress had ever tried a pinot noir based on her selections. Prices are decent though!

Some day, I'll go to Contra, but in the meanwhile, I'm happy to save some shekels and sample a bunch of things on Wildair's menu. The primary qualities in Wildair's favor: a great wine list with reasonably priced bottles (I didn't start feeling like a real adult until I ordered bottles with my dinner), a great set of experimental/creative small plates, and an unpretentious atmosphere. 

Our server was very knowledgeable about the wine menu and was able to recommend us an affordable, delicious pét-nat (Sébastien Brunet 100% Grolleau, 2013) when the wine we wanted wasn't available. We toasted our luck, then proceeded to destroy the bread plate. Yes, it's worth paying $4 for the warm, delicious bread and the super fruity dish of olive oil. They were out of the pork rilettes, but I'm sure that would have been great for bread-dipping, too.

We enjoyed the potato darphin with uni, which, like a challah BLT, is a little tongue-in-cheek (for those who don't keep kosher) -- it's a delicious latke/hashbrown with lightly pickled jalapenos and red onion. Weird mix of flavors, but the brininess of the uni was a great contrast to the earthy potato. The fried squid was a little less exciting, but still a lovely, tasty dish. There were more things we would have liked to order, but we had more eating to do.

The one misstep: the Georgia white shrimp still had shells, legs, and tails on -- it was flavorful and pretty, but made for a super messy eating experience at our tiny table. 

The service was attentive, the space was cute, and the menu offerings were tasty, easily shared, and prettily presented. This seems like a great date spot, but if you want the night to go on, don't get the shrimp -- it's just not a sexy look.
