If you prefer natural wines from small producers, you need to check out Willdair. 

All the food we tried was delicious, but even better was how well it went with our wine. Someone put a lot of thought into making a wine list and menu that are really in sync. 

Like most small-plates places, get at least one more dish than you think you'll need!

Wildair has a great reputation for tapas style dining with a unique flair and I must say its well deserved. Make sure to get here early before they open because they don't take reservations and people line up outside before it opens! 

The wine selection is obscure but good, make sure to ask your server for recommendations. I split my order with one other person and got a total of 5 dishes. 

Highlights include potato darphin uni and the cheese plate. We ordered the Georgia white shrimp, bread, and schnitzel as well. The potato darphin with uni was easily the star of the meal but the saltiness of the darphin slightly overpowered the umami of the uni. Wildair didn't skimp on the uni but slightly decreasing the thickness of the darphin will make it almost perfect. Slight nitpick but the uni was not as fresh as it should be, but I can hardly complain given the amount they give. 

One thing you can't miss is the chocolate hazelnut tart for dessert. The sweetness of the tart is balanced by the sea salt sprinkled on top with the crunchy slightly sweet shell. Perfect for sharing with one other, and a great finish to any meal. One suggestion is to slightly increase the size of the shell to balance the creaminess of the tart or to make it slightly more crumbly. Either way, very minor issues. 

Food is incredible, wine is on point, and dessert is delicious. Expect a wait of at least 1 hour during dinner prime time and come early to guarantee a seat!

"Drink the wild air's salubrity,"--Ralph Waldo Emerson's "Merlin's 
Song"

How much did I like Wildair you ask?  Enough to do some research to see what "Wildair" means...I still don't know (as it pertains to the name of this restaurant), but it did take me to this famous line in the Emerson poem above!

Salubrity means "favorable to promoting health or well being."...and this is where I'm going...

I can't speak for health, but the restaurant Wildair, completely takes me to a place of "well being."  Everything about it is a reminder of what I love about living in the City (which I don't, nor have ever done, but long to do!).  

The restaurant itself is tiny, 36 seats I believe, and as you may have seen online, this place is getting a lot of attention, and is pretty hard to get into unless you get there early...but it's worth it if you do...and that's what we did!

At 5:45 on a Tuesday; we were third in a small line that had set up outside (6pm open).  By 6:30 we heard them telling new customer's coming in that the wait was about 1.5-2 hours.

The food--Inventive, full flavor, excitement to your mouth, and brain!  We had many items mentioned on yelp as well as in pro-reviews.  They were all special in there own way.  Below are my favorites:

Fried squid, spring onion, lemon, basil--Perfectly fried, crispy and crackly coated, yet melt in your mouth squid, onion and lemon.  I have never eaten fried lemons before, and they were incredible.  The citrus bite is softened by the frying leaving perfect lemon flavor.  I can't describe the sauce it comes with other than to say it's a simple "creamy" accompaniment that adds to the dish.

Tuna, cabbage, potato--The waiter said, "this tastes like a Ruben, but not in a bad way!"...Yup...This is perfectly seared tuna, sitting on perfectly roasted potatoes (I'm not meaning to be boring using "perfectly" back to back here...it just is what it is), with charred cabbage and spices on top.  All of this sitting in a brown butter emulsion--Bite for bite, one of the best things I've had eaten in the past year!

We also had the Beef Tartare and two desserts--As good as you've heard or read about!

The wine-list isn't my thing, but it's very well executed for what they're going for.  I did find a glass that I enjoyed.

Atmosphere--brick walls, great music, open kitchen, tight tables, great energy--Not everyone's cup of tea--but perfect for me!

Good, but honestly not as memorable as I was hoping it would be.

We got there around 7 on a Friday night and was quoted an hour wait time - this was expected, and we just waited at a bar around the corner until we got a text that a table was open.

We had the bread, shrimp, beef tartare, fried squid, and a tuna dish - they didn't have the tuna toast on the menu that day, which I was looking forward to trying, but instead, a poached (I think, if I remember correctly) tuna with cabbage, chimichurri, and potatoes.

My favorite was the squid - it was so perfectly crispy and airy, done in a light tempura style.  I loved the fried lemon and basil...the squid sauce was ok.  Could have been more flavorful.

The beef tartare was my second favorite - the cheddar and chestnut were a nice, unique touch.

The Georgian shrimp with celery and cilantro was good, but nothing special.  They serve it head and shell on, which I like, but some people may not.

Tuna was quite bland...which actually was ok, because the rest of the things we ordered tended to be on the heavier side...but it not a dish I particularly enjoyed.  I appreciate nuanced, milder dishes, but I actually found this one underseasoned and again, bland.

For a restaurant that's been one of the most talked-about of 2015, I found the hostess and waiters very polite, professional, and not at all stuck up like at some other "hip" places.  However, there was one gentleman (owner? manager?) who was quite offputting and disruptive to our meal...he was hovering over my seat the entire time, talking to the table next to us.  I thought at first that he knew the people, but as time went on, it became clear that he was just chatting up the ladies.  I'm all for managers (or whoever) checking up on customers and getting feedback...but he only approached tables of women, in a way that was obviously so creepy and sad.  And when you're sitting at small, adjoining high-top tables, it was particularly rude, because he was literally breathing down my back the whole time, and wouldn't even move out of the way for me to get up, because he was so focused on impressing the women.

Anyways, rant over.  In sum, food was generally well done, although there was no one dish I'm clamoring to come back for.  Ambiance and service were great, aside from the one guy.

I liked this place but there were some serious service flaws.  Food was mostly quite good.  Oysters were terrible though.  Served way too warm and they tasted a bit nasty.  Loved the fried squid dish.  Beef tartare very good too.  The wine list is was esoteric and natural.  I literally recognized almost nothing on the list.  The service was terrible.  It took 30 minutes to get our check and the place is tiny.  I don't think I'll return.  Fun to try but it didn't wow.
Average food, below average wine, and understaffed. There are better wine bars in Manhattan without the long wait.
Overrated! 3 stars only because chef is talented and because that place can growing! I will come back to taste again..

Wildair was a little disappointing -- I didn't find the food very memorable. The staff and service were accommodating but they seemed understaffed. It took a long time to get our waiter's attention. The tables were a bit too squished together and it felt like we were sitting on top of each other. 

Bread & Olive Oil: Bread was uniquely dense with a nice crisp crust. 4/5
Pork Rillette: Decent consistency but lacked flavor 3/5
Cauliflower: Best thing we ordered there. Well cooked and delicious sauce 5/5
Beef Tartare: Bland and forgettable 2/5
Fried Squid: Well cooked. The paired sauce was a little dull 4/5
Panna Cotta: Weirdly deconstructed and the flavors didn't gell together 2/5

Service: 4/5
Ambiance: 2/5
Food: 3/5

Atmosphere...typical wine bar in NYC

Food: average, nothing great, but not bad

Grilled cauliflower: pretty tasty, but don't put too much sauce on it

Shrimp: good flavor but overcooked; the meat was mushy

Tuna tartar: can barely taste the tuna, too much sauce..marination was full of flavor

Beef tar tar: made well but definitely not the best I've had

Service: little more on the rude side vs friendly

They charged $4 for the bread...whaaaa?

4.5/4.75. A few small issues, but rounding up because the food and wine were out of this world. Like actually, I'm not sure if these things were created by earthlings. Order 40 of the spicy tuna plates. And maybe 30 of the beef tartares. Okay maybe just come here for dinner every night and deal with the whole going broke thing later. Sound reasoning, no?

Came here around 7:30 on a Thursday night. As others have reported, there's going to be a pretty substantial wait if you don't come between 6-6:30 (NO RESERVATIONS). The hostess was incredibly scattered, which was one of the minor issues we experienced during our visit. I'm not sure if she was overwhelmed or what, but there seemed to be no organization whatsoever when it came to seating people efficiently. So while our first impression wasn't good, we were determined to stick it out - thank god we did! The wait ended up being about 45 minutes (they told us 30), but we were rewarded for good behavior, being sat right in front of the kitchen! Some might prefer a table, but my fellow foodie friend and I were thrilled.

Just to clarify - when I say foodie, I'm not one of those voracious Times/Eater/Grub Street/Infatuation readers who knows everything about every restaurant opened by "this team" or "that team" or "the brainchild of the creators of so and so...". What I did know going into it was this: I had been wanting to try the tasting menu at Contra for quite some time, and when I heard that Wildair was the more causal - wait for it - BRAINCHILD of the Contra folks, and a la carte to boot, it shot up to the top of my list. 

First: Wine. I know cocktails very well, beer pretty well, and wine not well at all. So when I'm confronted with a wine list such as the colossal display at Wildair, I get really intimidated. Thankfully, there were plenty of servers around to help guide us in the right direction, and all of them were quite patient with our amateur-ism. I ended up trying two different reds which were both fantastic. We both opted for wine by the glass, so we were able to give our prospective options a taste before deciding. The wine here - along with being overwhelmingly diverse - is natural/organic/biodynamic, so like the food, the feel is very clean and refined. 

FOOD! The way that everything is listed on the menu, you'd think the food here is oddly minimalist. This is not the case. They list the key players in each dish, but the subtleties are left a mystery. I'm a fan. 

-Bread and Olive Oil (A)
Paying for bread seems silly to me. But they're known for making some standout bread in-house here, and the rumors are true. The only thing silly here would be NOT to order it. Not much more to say - you gotta experience it yourself. 

-Beef Tartare, Smoked Cheddar, Chestnuts (A+)
I don't eat red meat too often but after perusing the Yelp and the Google for a bit before coming here, it seemed pretty unanimous that ordering the beef tartare at Wildair might be the best decision you make all day. Again, the hype was warranted. The texture and flavor profiles of this dish were sublime. The tuna was my favorite dish of the meal, but my inner foodie knows this baby was by far the most inventive and beautifully-executed plate we had. Apparently, beef can be made light and fluffy - thank you Wildair for enlightening me. Just a note - this plate is slightly spicy thanks to the addition of some horseradish. This made the dish for me.

-Georgia White Shrimp, Celery, Cilantro (A)
You're encouraged to eat the skin. It's not necessary, but it made the dish for me. I wasn't head over heels in love with the shrimp honestly, but it was masterfully prepared, as everything here seems to be. 

-Spicy Tuna, Scallion, Tomatoes (A+++)
Served on toast. Party in your mouth good. I suppose it's not as "refined" as some of the other dishes here and certainly not as complex, but the resounding flavor is incredibly powerful. The tomato and tuna blend together in the sweetest of harmonies. Now that's what I call a power couple.

-Chocolate Hazelnut Tart (A++) 
I basically don't eat desserts because consuming food high in sugar does really weird stuff to my chemistry. That said, I caved and had a couple bites of the tart after hearing nothing but squeals of glee from my equally adventurous dining companion. They were warranted, I assure you. The tart looks quite simple. Deceptively simple. I don't know how they make this little piece of heaven taste so damn good (the salt on top doesn't hurt), but whatever they do, they better keep doing it. Sweet, rich, creamy but not too heavy.
Small thoughtful menu. Small expensive but delicious plates. Best shrimp I've ever had. Wine selection was fantastic. Ambient atmosphere but a bit cramped/crowded.

Came here on Halloween night for dinner to escape the parties & bar scene... seemed like a good night to do so because we got a 4-top table pretty quick!

The Pros:

- Fun dishes, good portions for sharing (favorite was the beef tartar)
- Great music
- Lots of gluten free options (most, if not all, without modification)
- Really nice staff
- The panna cotta!!!!!! (best I've ever had, and it was even modified to be GF)

The Cons:

- Wine list was a bit unapproachable... wasn't a fan of my rose or the first red we got... however the last bottle saved the night (recommended by our server)
- The shrimp dish... way too salty (and I love salt), and they failed to mention you could eat the shell... we spent a lot of messy minutes trying to peel & eat

I would love to try Contra next time I'm in NY, because Wildair was definitely a highlight for me!
The food was simple and well done. But the place is a little cramped and noisy, and service wasn't very attentive.
Nice LES spot, good wine options and inventive food. I prefered their flagship spot Contra next door, but for a more laid-back date this is a casual place that is worth the visit.

KenScale: 8.5/10

Wildair is the second project behind the Contra team duo of chefs Jeremiah Stone and Fabian von Hauske right next to Contra. Unlike Contra, which showcases inventive and affordable tasting menus, Wildair has even more casual wine bar setting serving food a la carte. Lately, natural/biodynamic wine movement is all the rage in NYC, and Wildiar is one of the leaders on that front. Honestly, I really didn't get the hype behind these types of wine as I generally found them to be on the bland side without full range of flavor from ordinary wines. On the other hand, Wildair is a successful sophomore project in the food department. I was very impressed with many dishes here that are somewhat loosened up compared to Contra yet still display versatility in flavor and texture. 

I've had beef tartare in dozens of restaurants in NYC by now, but the one at Wildiar is definitely a class on its own (almost on par with my favorite at Estela). The texture of tartare was spot-on (further enhanced by crunchy chestnut), and the combination of smoked cheddar added another dimension to flavor. Fried squid was not another calamari-type dish. It was so crispy with no hint of sogginess and the combination of spring onion, lemon and basil made for delightful sensation to my palate. Georgia white shrimp was another winner, with fresh shrimp accompanied by celery and cilantro to create unique flavor that didn't overwhelm the shrimp itself. Pork Milanese looks like another pork cutlet, but it was more or less perfectly cooked and worked very well with gribiche sauce. For dessert, chocolate peanut tart, as ordinary as it sounds, was a revelation, with flavor that was elegant without being overly sweet. 

Wildair doesn't accept reservations, and the place is as hot as ever, especially after favorable reviews from professional critics starting falling in, so make sure to come by early. I showed up slight after 8 p.m. on a Tuesday night and still had to wait around an hour to get seated. I liked the lively vibe of the dining area with high tables where you can chat with your friends in a relaxed setting. As noted above, the restaurant only serves natural/biodynamic wine, so if that's your thing, you're definitely at the right place. Wildair is another welcome addition to NYC's dining scene, and this is the type of place I would be happy to take out my friends over and over again, with creative but not-over-the-top food that will make for a very pleasant dinner.

Save your self time deciding and just order the whole menu. My friend has a serious shellfish allergy and after falling in mouth lust with everything non shellfish that we ordered, I silently cursed him for his non-mermaid genetics in my mind. Ordering everything will keep friendships in tact. Wine too.

Food delic... but even "diner basic" rules of service were ignored - my wine glass sat empty since appetizer, no silver change between courses, no one checked on me-ever despite sitting at chef's bar... I felt so ignored I could have dined and ditched. Hope front of house improves to level of back as food was carefully and skillfully prepared. Props to the hostess - she was great!

An amazing lower Eastside gem! Casual enough for a low key Tuesday evening or perfect for a Friday night to kick it with friends. My favorite dishes are the shrimp, the pork rillette and the fried squid! Jorge works wonders and always has a phenomenal recommendation from the eclectic list of delicious wines. I love the friendly staff and warm vibes.

IN SHORT: Casual, inventive, small plates from two talented, young chefs in a space that blurs the distinction between restaurant and wine bar.

THE STORY: In March of this year, I wrote about Contra, the first, tasting-menu-only restaurant by the young, boundary-pushing duo of Jeremiah Stone and Fabian von Hauske. I called it a sophisticated, subtly innovative restaurant so well suited to a youthful New York culinary scene, and though the price of 5-courses has since moved from $55 up to $67 this season, the ambition and the sensibility behind the restaurant is still there.

In June, the pair then opened Wildair, a slightly more casual space, offering an à la carte dinner menu just a couple doors down on a quietly gritty stretch of Orchard Street. And as is true of a great oeuvre in a great discipline, both restaurants are made better by the other's existence.

Where Contra is disciplined and restrained, the no-reservations Wildair is brave and informal. The chefs seem to have relaxed their cooking and now apply salt, fat, and spice with a more freewheeling hand, and it is for the benefit of all. The tender morsels of beef tartare were made rich from ethereal ribbons of smoked cheddar and chesnut, and then quickly made spicy by just the right hit of horseradish. With crispy barley scattered on top, it is a dish made by chefs with an almost unparalleled intuition for what is perfectly fresh, natural, and seasonal, and yet the depth of flavor is more profound than imaginable.

The spicy tuna on toast topped with tomatoes of an identical hue is slightly less successful, with the briny scallion that tastes of seaweed too strong a flavor to sit next to the delicate fish. It is, however, just a rare unfortunate incident when one novel, conceptual flavor wins out at the expense of others.

Yet in the whole Georgia white shrimp, served heads-on with celery and cilantro, adventure and experimentation return, and bold, oily, spicy flavors zing around the palette. The plate feels like an evolution of the chefs' more emphatically New Nordic inspiration taken at Contra, presenting a meal here of whole, scavenged ingredients treated with a breathless, expressive energy.

As at Contra, Chef von Hauske's "bread and butter service" is still exceptional, most recently presenting a gloriously dense and chewy roll with a crackling crust. However, the dish that possibly best represents Wildair is the fried squid. Here, the chefs have lightly fried in what is ultimately an airy skin both tender bites of squid and barely preserved slices of lemon. After a surprising bite of the fried lemon, the acidity and bittersweetness linger, and the next bite of squid, dipped in a rich, dark aioli stained with ink, becomes even brighter and more deliciously energetic. The dish in its entirety embodies the earnest, experimental approach at Wildair, where culinary norms are upended with gentle, contemporary moves.

The space itself has also been designed with a neutral attitude on what form the experience of going out to dinner should take. The narrow, 45-seat space is divided into two long rows of bar-height tables with four additional seats on a counter facing directly into the open kitchen, and the long, modern, heavily French wine list offers many the option of just enjoying a drink while perhaps nibbling on a small snack from the menu. Others will be squeezing 5 or 6 larger dishes onto their table, eagerly making a full dinner last for 2 hours. It is almost as if the restaurant wants to scream that it is "For the People!", whoever they might be.

The chefs are young and they are exceedingly talented, and thus the food is focused and energetic, the restaurant honest and transparent in turn. Indeed, Wildair is a great work in a great discipline, a great addition to dining in the Lower East Side, a great addition to the young, modern New York we know.

The food here is inventive, cooked intelligently, and yet, it still feels similar and comfortable. The fried squid may be one of the best things I've had in a long while. The desserts, one a chocolate/hazelnut tart and another a panna cotta, are excellent ways to end a meal. The price point in all aspects, from appetizers to cocktails, are also spot on - affordable even.

Beyond what others are saying about the food, I particularly enjoyed the details of the decor and ambience. Look up and around you, and you'll notice the design details (again the intelligence put into the experience). The music just made me want to hang out there and have a good time.

Wildair - you are officially one of my favorite places now in NYC.

The people who work there are so friendly, down to earth, and they easily make you feel very welcomed.  They paid attention to little service details, down to putting the merchants copy receipt on top of the customer copy.  

The reason for the 5 stars is that I've been to Wildair twice and had two amazing meals.  Every single dish was delicious; there wasn't one that fell flat.  I also liked the order in which they served everything from lightest to spiciest.  

Everyone raves about the bread and olive oil, and yes... you should absolutely pay $4 for this.  The bread is everything everyone says it is: warm, soft on the inside, hard on the outside.  The other dishes are small, so you mostly get full on the bread.

Scallop Crudo - My sister's favorite.  They had slices of grapefruit mixed in there with kale and cucumber.  I love cooked scallops, and normally don't get the crudo, but this dish had me rethinking my stance

Beef Tartare - The cheddar wasn't overwhelming like I find most cheese toppings, but just the right amount was added. This was my favorite dish.  The beef was finely chopped and managed to feel airy.

Spicy Tuna - This is served on toast and definitely has a kick to it.  

In total, we spent about $50.  The first time, my friend and I ordered wine which was delicious and super reasonable.  Wildair has a fantastic wine list, and the servers are very knowledgeable about what pairs well with certain dishes.  

Highly recommend coming here.

It was ok. They are trying to be creative, but some dishes just weren't executed well.

The food is a mixed bag. The good: the bread and olive oil (bread was dense, soft, and tasty; olive oil was incredibly flavorful), and the crudo (delicious and creative - what we were hoping the whole menu would be like). The other dishes we tried were just ok: shrimp with celery and cilantro (flavors weren't blended, so you had to get each of the component bits on your fork every time), and the pork milanese (fried pork, tasty but nothing special). I would give the good dishes 5 stars, and the other dishes 2 stars.

Service was great, until a large table came and then it was crappy.

Ambiance is casual.

We went to Contra before and found some dishes were fantastic while others were mediocre. Wildair was the same. There are so many restaurants in the city whose menus are all good, Wildair isn't worth the "risk".

I'm conflicted about this place. Went last night after seeing the 4 star review in Time Out NY and it definitely didn't live up to their normal standard for a 4 star new restaurant. However, some of the dishes we had were absolutely fantastic and maybe, as a new restaurant they just need to work through a few kinks. 

Let's start with the good:

The bread and olive oil was delicious. Seemed freshly baked and tasted like sourdough (which I love).

Scallop Crudo OMG fantastic. One of the best scallop dishes I've had. The scallop was pillowy soft with a refreshing citrus and cucumber sauce on top. Delicious. 

Spicy Tuna-another win. Sort of like a elevated spicy tuna roll on toasted bread which added a nice smokey flavor and crunchy texture. Loved this dish.

Beef Tartar-solid dish. I think my expectations were a bit too high considering the Time Out review highlighted this specific dish. It was very good but didn't stand out to me like the spicy Tuna and the scallop did.

The so-so:

Radishes with seaweed butter. It was ok, but nothing really special. Wouldn't order it again.

The cheese plate-we had this for dessert (which seemed to confuse our waiter). The cheeses were actually quite good but they don't come with anything. Like, no bread, no almonds, no honey. It's literally just some slices of cheese. If you're going to offer this, just make it a buck or two more and throw in some slices of bread....

The bad:

Our waiter seemed a bit rushed. He forgot one of our dishes which, I know happens but I think they just need to hire more front-house staff. 

The wine list-I drink my far share of wine but I'm no Dionysus. I was completely lost with this wine list which pretty much only features small growers and lesser known varieties. The people next to us seemed to be stumped as well so I know it's not just me. 

I asked for a rec on the closest white by the glass to a sauvignon blanc and got a vouvrey which was a bit too acidic for my taste, especially for the $15 a pop price. We then moved on to the Pet Nat section of the list (yea we had to google what that was. Don't judge) and got a glass of the dry sparkling stuff which wasn't stellar but did the trick. I'm all about trying new things (esp drinks) but if they're going to put forward a wine list that might not be familiar at all to people, it may be good to have some short descriptions, at least for the wine by the glass, so that people aren't completely lost. Take Terrior Wine bar for example, lots of lesser known wines but great descriptions which help you navigate. 


All and I I would go back, maybe in a few months when, hopefully, they have some of the issues mentioned above worked out.

The food here was pretty good and we didn't have to wait in line at all when we got here around 6:30ish. 

Food:
Oysters with lemons - delicious and fresh
Scallops crudo - very good but I'm not a huge fan of the grapefruit and some of the veggies in this dish
Beef tartare with cheese - delicious 
Summer squash - not good; too bland; wouldn't order this again
Wagyu steak - yummy
Panna cotta with peach granita and crumbs - the peach granita was on the sour/bitter side but the rest of the dessert was good

One of the best meals I've had an ages. Have had beef tartare at all the top spots in the city and this is hands down the tastiest, leaving estela in the dust. Scallops crudo were also next level, as were the saldines and nuanced hazelnut chocolate torte

Also reasonably priced! Just go already
The food is well prepared but not outstanding. This place is a fun place to eat but it is not worthy of the over the top admiration it receives. The wine list is nice and well priced.

Fantastic dining experience! 

Where do I start? Let's start with the well curated wine list. It consist of mostly natural wine from small wine makers. We started with the extra refreshing  spritzer. Followed by a beautiful white blends from Cantina Giardino, which really opens up our palette. 

For food, we started with the oysters on the half shell pair with bone-dry muscadet  - perfect to go with the salty briny oysters. Comes the appetizer - mangalitsa soppresata, some amazing salami. It is richer sweeter than regular salami because of the mangalitsa pig. It is paired with the most wonderful Laurence & Remi Dufaitre. 

Oh how can I forget the beef tartar with mustard seeds and smoked cheddar. And the marvelous roasted sardine with grilled eggplant, feta and green olive. This is my favorite of the night. It's bustling with favors in multiple directions - smoky salty sweet . Oh mine!

And it gets better and better. The giant Georgia white shrimp simply seasoned with soy sauce decorated with cilantro and celery. This is outstanding. The shrimp was charged outside that you can eat the shrimp whole with the crispy shell.  

Now comes the wagyu steak for two. This is heavenly. Juicy scrumptiousness paired with sweet charred shallot and shishito. It paired well with the  C'est le Printemps Crozes Hermitage Syrah which is youthful and bouncing of black cherry and hung of honey nites. I had a foodgasome right there.

At last we decided not to skip the hazelnut chocolate tart regardless we were beyond full. Boy what a smart choice we made

I have been to the sister restaurant - Contra multiple times. While it is equally outstanding, I prefer the wine bar theme at Wildair more. 

Last note. If you get lost in the wine list, don't hesitate to ask Jorge, the wine manager. Trust the man , if you don't know what you want.

"I just high fived the man for his wine choices -- ridiculous."  

Orange wine is now top of mind and my charts on gem discoveries, along with Wildair -- a truly kick ass place to get your munch on and slake the vino beast. 

It was an exceptional night of creative dishes, perfect pairings, seamless service & casual feasting with my old friend Chad and a great server --  Michael.  I'm still drunk from the evening, thank you, Michael. 

It was a balmy night yet the humid City was slashed to oblivion by steak tartar and seven more beauty dishes that kept coming as each equaled the last in its ability to provoke further hunger. My buddy Chad is an über foodie, and he just may have proven that following the kitchen's lead is the way to hit it. 

Tasty, fun, innovative & eye opening --
what more should a menu provide?

I'll be back for more wildness sho 'nuff.

Fake reviews piss me off.  This place is not worth a trip.

The menu is quite limited.  There are a number of appetizers and that's what they are - not tapas designed to be paired as an entree.  But then literally two entree choices, pork or steak.  Diverse, I know.

The service, while nice, is so slow it is like you're a prisoner - it was an Hour between appetizer and entree and then an hour between dessert and check even though we gave our card...

Finally the steak, which is one of two entree choices, was oversalted as was the broccoli side dish (appetizer ordered as side dish).

Save yourself the trouble.  This is a bar with snacks.  Oh and the wine list is ok albeit esoteric and they have one beer on the menu...
The clam toast is amazing. Would also come back for the fried squid (which includes thinly sliced fried lemon slices)!

Ok first of all, if you haven't been here or Contra, punch yourself in the face!

Jeremiah Stone and Fabian von Hauske dreamt up these sister eateries and have really done a bang-up job. Though this review is mainly for Wildair, I will say that the attention to detail, the warmth and inviting nature of the spaces, and (of course) the food is on-point as fuck for both places. On the night I was there, it was apparent to me that Jeremiah is a hustler--there is no shared kitchen, so he is literally Benny Hilling out the door and into the next to keep operations running smoothly.

EXTENSIVE and choice wine list. Incredible in-house baked, still-warm, chewy and savory bread. Delicious radishes sitting perfectly in delicious seaweed butter (did I taste matcha up in there?!!). Beautiful shrimp with a dreamy adornment of lime, fennel, celery. Spigarello!!! It's a broccoli rabe heirloom, you peasant! Put it in your mouth!

Before I left, I had to tell Jeremiah myself that the most amazing part of this experience was the rhubarb custard. Shut. Up. I can't even do it justice. Go try some. In fact, try it twice. At the beginning of your meal AND at the end. 

I can't wait for the next time I roll through here. It's a good place to keep in mind for needing a quick little snack, or a meal to satisfy a variety of cravings, or a magnum of wine. Or two bowls of rhubarb custard. 

(If I have any criticism at all, it's the lighting. I wish it was just a touch warmer?)

Great wine selection and delicious food in a very casual setting.

Highly recommend it! Pro tip: take the hazelnut tart

questions.question: I've tried calling them and they never pick up and they don't answer emails. Are any of their items available for pick up? I'm especially interested in their dessert.
questions.answer: Order for pick up on their website! I don't think they take orders over the phone. The donuts if that's what you are looking for are only available Friday and Saturday they release them at noon and usually sell out pretty fast.

questions.question: Seems difficult to get a reservation here. Has anyone been able to walk-in and get a seat at the bar to eat?
questions.answer: Three of us recently got seats early on Sunday.  Walk in.  Probably because few people know they are serving then.
